magic.name: The Arm of Ares
magic.desc:
Can be used as an druidic focus, +1 to spell attack rolls and save DC for Druid Spells.

Twice Per Day, the wielder can ritually cast (10 minutes) the *Speak with Plants* spell.

Also, as an action, the wielder can plant the staff into the ground. The staff grows and into a nonmagical Giant Mushroom. The mushroom is 60 feet tall and has a 5-foot-diameter stem, and its cap at the top spreads out in a 20-foot radius. Any creatures occupying the same space as the staff as it grows will be pushed vertically atop the mushroom. Additionally, all creatures who finish their turn *underneath* the mushroom inhale spore's released from the mushrooms cap, and must succeed on a *DC 16 Consitution Saving Throw*, or have the *Incapacitated* condition. *Incapacitated* creatures repeat the save at the start of their next 3 turn's, otherwise waking up naturally after 3 turns have passed.
The giant mushroom fully decays after spending more than 1 hour in sunlight, otherwise the mushroom will last for 3d6 days.

To use this feature again, the staff must be planted in the ground of the *Underdark*, where it replenishes its mycelial energy from the ground, taking a long rest to recharge.

magic.name: Magebane Bolas
magic.desc: You can make a ranged weapon attack with these bolas against a Large or smaller target. When you do, you throw the bolas at the target; on a hit, the target takes the *1d4 bludgeoning* damage, and it must succeed on a Strength saving throw (*DC = 8 + Dex + Prof*) or be knocked prone and entangled by the bolas. If the target has the ability to cast spells, they subtract *1d6* from this save and future saves made attempting to escape the bolas. While entangled in this way, the target's has the *restrained* condition, and is unable to speak. The target remains entangled until it's freed. A creature can use its action to make a *DC = (8 + Int + Prof)* Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within reach on a success. If the target has the *Spellcasting* or *Pact-Magic* feature, the *DC* becomes (*10 + Int + Prof*).

magic.name: Sussur Dagger
magic.desc:
On a successful attack roll, the target must make a constitution saving throw using your save DC or have the silenced condition (unable to speak or use verbal components of spells) until the end of their next turn.
Additionally, the dagger emits a dim light (5ft) in the prescence of immediate magic (10ft).

magic.name: Ring of the Cosmos
magic.desc:
Looking into the main gemstone of this ring shows the landscape of one of the Planes, which changes daily. To determine the plane, roll 1d8 at dusk (provided you are on the Material Plane) and consult the table below. (Note, if you are on any of the planes listed, the ring automatically shows a landscape from the plane you are present on).

| 1d8 | Plane | Creature Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Astral Sea | Aberration |
| 2 | Shadowfell | Undead |
| 3 | Feywild | Fey |
| 4 | The 9 Hells | Fiend |
| 5 | The Triad of the Heavens | Celestial |
| 6 | The Eternal Forge | Construct |
| 7 | Mount Vertaei | Humanoid, Giant |
| 8 | Azeros' Comet | Elemental |

1/Dawn, you can use a *magic action* to transform into a creature of the type listed next to the plane of CR less than or equal to your level divided by 3 (round down). When you do this, you retain your Hit Points, Hit Dice, proficiencies, personality, and ability to communicate. Your alignment also stays the same, but is influenced somewhat by the creature you transform into, finding yourself occasionally wanting to do similar things to the chosen creature. You choose if you retain your mental stats (INT, WIS, CHA) or take the creatures.

You Do Not gain the creatures Legendary Resistances, Condition Immunities, Initiative Bonus or Regional Effects if there are any.

Upon shape-shifting, you determine whether your equipment drops to the ground or changes in size and shape to fit the new form while you're in it, with the exce

magic.name: Eye of the Watcher
magic.desc:
While you are attuned to this item, you can cast *see invisibility* on yourself at will.

*Curse.* When you attune to the Eye of The Watcher, you are suddenly overcome with the urge to see what it sees. Make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you're able to resist the enchantment and are aware of the curse's effects, but are not attuned to it. On a failure, you forcefully tear out one of your own Eyes, taking 4d10 necrotic damage, allowing the Eye of The Watcher to crawl into its place. If you are already missing an Eye, you are simply compelled to allow the Eye to crawl into the empty socket.

You can see normally while the Eye of The Watcher remains in your socket, but can choose to close your other Eye to see through its magically enhanced lens using a bonus action. Looking through the Eye grants you darkvision of up to 120 feet, and are able to peer through both magical and nonmagical darkness using it. The Eye moves slower than a normal Eye, leaving slight trails and motion blurs behind it as you look through it. While looking only through the Eye of The Watcher, you have disadvantage on any attack you make as well as ability checks that rely on depth perception. You can open your other Eye and regain your normal vision using another bonus action.

*The Watcher familiar.* The Eye is a gruesome familiar. As an action, you can command the Eye to crawl out of its socket and move independently of you. Use the abilities described in the *find familiar* spell when comm

magic.name: Aboleth Brain
magic.desc:
*The Brain of a young Aboleth, tainted by an otherwordly power.* The brain can be consumed, granting the following bonuses:

Otherwordly Memories
Your mind becomes flooded with cosmic memories that aren't your own. Once per day, you may attempt to call upon these memories to try and glean some information about a particular item, place, creature or course of action by making a Wisdom saving throw.
On a 20+, you may ask the DM one question, and receive a vague but truthful answer, provided the answer is within these memories. If it is not, the daily use of this feature is not consumed.
On a 15-19, you may ask the DM one question, and receive a vision associated with the question asked, provided the answer is within these memories.
On a 14 or lower, you take 3d8 psychic damage and have the stunned condition for 1 minute, as your mind is flooded with incomprehensible thoughts.

Improved Mutations
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with your organic weapons.

Devouring Urge
Once per turn when you hit a creature with your organic weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic or Psychic damage (your choice) to the creature, and you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice to roll it and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point). In addition, the flesh consumed by the creature temporarily alters your form. The DM will either:
Grant you a temporary mutation of the DM's choice, which last for 1 minute. Using this fea

magic.name: Amulet of the Watcher
magic.desc:
Gain +1 to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.
Gain proficiency in perception. If you already have proficiency, gain expertise instead.

Additionally, as an action, you can place up to two spectral eyes (only visible with a DC20 Perception or DC15 Arcana check) firmly on a solid surface-such as a wall, table, or boot-where it remains until destroyed. While you're within 5 feet of an eye, you can use a bonus action to speak the command word to cause its eye to open. The opening is about the size of a keyhole, and by peering through it, you can open and see through another eye's opening of your choice. You choose which eye to look through the first time you peer into the hole and can change it again using a bonus action. If another eye is placed when two are already active, the eye that was placed *first* dissapears in a non-harmful yet visible & audible explosion of blue light.

The eyes you can choose to see through in this way must be a part of the set, be placed on a solid surface, and be on the same plane of existence as the one you're looking through. You can only see through one eye at a time, which operates both ways, and nothing can pass through the hole. If another eye attempts to look through one you're already using, the connection between the first two ends and is replaced by the new one. An eye closes when it's no longer being looked through.

Each eye has AC 10 and 5 hit points. If it drops to 0 hit points, the eye is destroyed. If a ta

magic.name: The Lucky Marksman
magic.desc:
*Hitting headshots is very hard. So I shoot a target the size of a coin instead*

This magic revolver has 1d4 charges (maximum of 4) and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. While attuned to this weapon, you possess a number of golden coins equal to the number of charges currently available.

*Ricochet.* When you take the Attack action and make a ranged attack with this weapon, rather than attacking a creature normally you can expend 1 charge to toss one of the golden coins into the air at a point you can see within 30 feet of you. The coin occupies that space until the attack is resolved. Instead of targeting a creature, you make the attack roll against the coin (AC 20). The coin is a Tiny object.

If you hit the coin, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of the coin as the original target of the attack. After determining that the coin is hit, flip a coin:
- Heads: The bullet ricochets off of the coin and deals an extra 2d8 radiant damage
- Tails: The bullet splits into two & ricochets into a second creature within 30ft of the coin. Make a new attack roll against that creature.

Both the Heads & Tails properties ignore half cover and three-quarters cover if the coin has a clear line of sight to the target.
If you critically hit the coin, the attack gains the benefits of both Heads and Tails.

The coin falls harmlessly to the ground immediately after the attack is resolved, and disappears after 1 minute.

*Magic Reload.* When you use a Bonus Action to reload th

magic.name: Unstable Feywild Crystal
magic.desc:
This warm crystal glints with the sunset colors of the Feywild sky and evokes whispers of emotional memory. As an action, you can attach the shard to a Tiny object (such as a weapon or a piece of jewelry) or detach it. It falls off if your attunement to it ends. You can use the shard as a spellcasting focus while you hold or wear it.

You can channel the forces of chance and chaos from the Feywild to gain Advantage on one d20 Test. Once you do so, you must finish a Long Rest before you can use this feature again.

Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot before you regain the use of this feature, you automatically roll on the Wild Magic Surge table and regain the use of this feature. This can be done 1 + (Proficiency Bonus) times per long rest.

*It looks like it could be forged into something greater...*

magic.name: Blade of the Chosen
magic.desc:
A Magical Weapon said to have been forged by Druenol himself, that has been bestowed upon only the greatest warriors for generations, destined by fate. After attuning to the weapon, the weapon shifts into a Melee Simple or Martial weapon of the user's choice, and cannot change after attuning to the user.

You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 7 runes inscribed into it.
In Darkness, the unsheathed weapon sheds moonlight, creating Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet.

Rune 1: Dormant
Rune 2: Dormant
Rune 3: Dormant
Rune 4: Dormant
Rune 5: Dormant
Rune 6: Dormant
Rune 7: Dormant

magic.name: Genie's Vessel
magic.desc:
A magical Tiny vessel that serves as a spellcasting focus for warlock spells. Its AC equals the wielder's spell save DC ({{VESSEL_AC}}), and it has Hit Points equal to their warlock level + their Proficiency Bonus ({{VESSEL_HP}}). If destroyed or lost, it can be replaced with a 1-hour ceremony during a rest. Its exact form depends on the warlock's Genie Kind - a brass bottle, a woven basket, a jeweled flask, a shattered flagon, or similar.

Bottled Respite: the vessel's extradimensional space is a 20-ft-radius, 20-ft-high cylinder. Items left inside remain there until taken out or the vessel is destroyed - functionally the same as a Bag of Holding for storage purposes.

magic.name: Potion of Polymorphine
magic.desc:
When you drink this potion, the DM rolls a random creature with a challenge rating in the 0-1 band (examples at this tier include a rat, a goat, a wolf, a giant frog, or a black bear) and you become that creature's stat block exactly. Any items, objects, and treasure you were carrying meld into your soul and return once the polymorphine wears off.

This form lasts 1d4 hours. Drinking another potion of polymorphine while already under this effect extends the duration by a further 1d6 hours. Remaining polymorphed for too long may have unforeseen side effects.

While polymorphed by this potion, if you drop to 0 hit points you die outright instead of making death saving throws. If you die while under this effect, you revert to your original form once your remaining duration elapses.

magic.name: Ashbringer
magic.desc:
Infused with the Holy Light and forged by King Magni Bronzebeard on the Great Anvil of Ironforge, Ashbringer was once the pride and joy of the knightly Mograine family. But when the traitorous Renault Mograine used the sword to kill his father, it became corrupted. The sword was claimed by the Scourge until Renault's brother, Darion Mograine, betrayed the Lich King and delivered the weapon to Tirion Fordring—an act of heroism that cleansed Ashbringer of its corruption and restored the sword to its rightful form.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It deals an extra 1d10 Fire damage on a hit, or an extra 3d10 Fire damage if the target is Undead.

Changing States. When first encountered, Ashbringer is in either its True State or its Corrupted State. At the DM's discretion, Ashbringer changes into its Corrupted State if its wielder uses it to commit an act of legendary wickedness; it changes into its True State if its wielder uses it to commit an act of legendary heroism. Ashbringer's current state grants you one of the following benefits:

Steal Life (Corrupted State Only). Whenever you use Ashbringer to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you gain 20 Temporary Hit Points.

Wake of Ashes (True State Only). Whenever you use Ashbringer to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you can make its corpse explode into a cloud of smoldering ash. Each creature of your choice in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the target must s

magic.name: Ashen Bands of Courage
magic.desc:
This metal band is adorned with five gleaming crystals suggesting a beast's claw. The forge mark of Ormus the Penitent—a stylized O—is imprinted inside the band.

Ashen Band of Courage (Uncommon, Requires Renown 3+). While wearing this ring, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

Ashen Band of Greater Courage (Rare, Requires Renown 10+). In addition to the Uncommon property, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while wearing this ring.

Ashen Band of Unmatched Courage (Very Rare, Requires Renown 25+). In addition to the Uncommon and Rare properties, you gain a +1 bonus to saving throws while wearing this ring.

Ashen Band of Endless Courage (Legendary, Requires Renown 50+). In addition to the Rare and Very Rare properties, you have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions while wearing this ring.

Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

- Ashen Band of Courage
- Ashen Band of Greater Courage
- Ashen Band of Unmatched Courage
- Ashen Band of Endless Courage

magic.name: Ashen Bands of Destruction
magic.desc:
This thick metal band is adorned with a skull design, with two luminous blue gems serving as eyes. The forge mark of Ormus the Penitent—a stylized O—is imprinted inside the band.

Ashen Band of Destruction (Uncommon, Requires Renown 3+). While wearing this ring, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls, and your spell saving throw DC increases by 1.

Ashen Band of Greater Destruction (Rare, Requires Renown 10+). The bonus to attack rolls and increase to saving throw DC increase to +2.

Ashen Band of Unmatched Destruction (Very Rare, Requires Renown 25+). The bonus to attack rolls and increase to saving throw DC increase to +3. In addition, you can treat any 1 you roll on a damage die for a spell you cast as a 2 while wearing this ring.

Ashen Band of Endless Destruction (Charisma, Intelligence, or Wisdom) (Legendary, Requires Renown 50+). In addition to the Very Rare property, your spellcasting ability increases by 2 (to a maximum of 30) while wearing this ring. You can also add a +3 bonus to one damage roll of each spell you cast.

Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

- Ashen Band of Destruction
- Ashen Band of Greater Destruction
- Ashen Band of Unmatched Destruction
- Ashen Band of Endless Destruction

magic.name: Ashen Bands of Might
magic.desc:
This metal band is adorned with a stylized helm design, with purple gems forming the nose guard and crest. The forge mark of Ormus the Penitent—a stylized O—is imprinted inside the band.

Ashen Band of Might (Uncommon, Requires Renown 3+). While wearing this ring, you gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls for melee weapon attacks.

Ashen Band of Greater Might (Rare, Requires Renown 10+). In addition to the Uncommon property, your Strength is 19 while you're wearing this ring. This property has no effect if your Strength is 19 or higher without it.

Ashen Band of Unmatched Might (Very Rare, Requires Renown 25+). In addition to the Uncommon property, your Strength is 21 while you're wearing this ring. This property has no effect if your Strength is 21 or higher without it. In addition, you can treat any 1 you roll on a melee weapon's damage die as a 2.

Ashen Band of Endless Might (Legendary, Requires Renown 50+). In addition to the Uncommon and Very Rare properties, your Strength is 25 while you're wearing this ring. This property has no effect if your Strength is 25 or higher without it.

Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

- Ashen Band of Might
- Ashen Band of Greater Might
- Ashen Band of Unmatched Might
- Ashen Band of Endless Might

magic.name: Ashen Bands of Vengeance
magic.desc:
This metal band is adorned with a stylized helm design, with deep-blue gems forming the nose guard and crest. The forge mark of Ormus the Penitent—a stylized O—is imprinted inside the band.

Ashen Band of Vengeance (Uncommon, Requires Renown 3+). While wearing this ring, you ignore Half Cover when making a ranged weapon attack roll, and you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls made with ranged weapons.

Ashen Band of Greater Vengeance (Rare, Requires Renown 10+). In addition to the Uncommon property, while you're wearing this ring, using a ranged weapon at long range doesn't impose Disadvantage on your attack roll.

Ashen Band of Unmatched Vengeance (Very Rare, Requires Renown 25+). In addition to the Uncommon and Rare properties, while wearing this ring, you ignore Three-Quarters Cover when making a ranged attack roll, and the maximum range of your ranged weapon attacks is doubled.

Ashen Band of Endless Vengeance (Legendary, Requires Renown 50+). In addition to the Uncommon, Rare, and Very Rare properties, while wearing this ring, you can treat any 1 or 2 you roll on a ranged weapon's damage die as a 3.

Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

- Ashen Band of Vengeance
- Ashen Band of Greater Vengeance
- Ashen Band of Unmatched Vengeance
- Ashen Band of Endless Vengeance

magic.name: Ashen Bands of Wisdom
magic.desc:
This metal band is adorned with an oval design suggestive of an eye, with a luminous turquoise stone at the center. The forge mark of Ormus the Penitent—a stylized O—is imprinted inside the band.

Ashen Band of Wisdom (Uncommon, Requires Renown 3+). While wearing this ring, you can treat any 1 you roll on a die to restore Hit Points to yourself or another creature as a 2.

Ashen Band of Greater Wisdom (Rare, Requires Renown 10+). In addition to the Uncommon property, whenever an effect you create restores Hit Points to one creature while you're wearing this ring, you can choose another creature within 30 feet of the first to also regain half that many Hit Points (round down).

Ashen Band of Unmatched Wisdom (Very Rare, Requires Renown 25+). In addition to the Uncommon and Rare properties, when you cast a spell with a range of touch that doesn't require an attack roll while wearing this ring, you can increase the spell's range to 30 feet.

Ashen Band of Endless Wisdom (Charisma, Intelligence, or Wisdom) (Legendary, Requires Renown 50+). In addition to the Uncommon, Rare, and Very Rare properties, your spellcasting ability also increases by 2 (to a maximum of 30) while you're wearing this ring.

Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

- Ashen Band of Wisdom
- Ashen Band of Greater Wisdom
- Ashen Band of Unmatched Wisdom
- Ashen Band of Endless Wisdom

magic.name: Aviana's Feather
magic.desc:
While attuned to this golden feather, you can take a Magic action to sprout a pair of glowing, golden wings from your back. The wings give you a Fly Speed of 80 feet, and any creature that makes an Opportunity Attack against you when you fly out of its reach has Disadvantage on the attack roll. If you fall while you have the wings, you descend at a rate of 60 feet per round until you land.

The wings last until you end the effect early as a Magic action or until your Attunement ends. If you are aloft when the wings disappear, you fall.

magic.name: Bauble of True Blood
magic.desc:
The red pendant on this necklace has 9 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. You can also expend Hit Point Dice when you finish a Short or Long Rest to replenish its charges, with each Hit Die you expend contributing 1 charge.

You can expend any number of charges to cast Cure Wounds from the bauble, with the number of charges determining the level of the spell (maximum of 9 charges for a level 9 spell).

magic.name: Bloodvenom Blade
magic.desc:
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, it deals an extra 2d6 Poison damage to any creature it hits, and the creature has the Poisoned condition until the start of your next turn.

Versatile. A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Mastery: Sap. If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

magic.name: Crown of the Ogre King
magic.desc:
While wearing this crown, you can take a Magic action to release a powerful belch that can be heard up to 300 feet away. Each creature in a 20-foot Cone originating from you makes a DC 17 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is pushed up to 20 feet away from you and has the Prone condition.

Cursed. This item is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic. Removing the crown fails to end the curse on you. While cursed, you are far hungrier than normal. You lose all your table manners, and your daily food requirement triples.

magic.name: Defias Leather
magic.desc:
Elite members of the Defias Brotherhood wear this armor to honor the faction's stonemason founders. While wearing the armor, you gain the following benefits.

Mason's Camouflage. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide behind stone objects and structures.

Meld into Stone. You can cast Meld into Stone from the armor. Once the armor has been used to cast this spell, it can't be used to cast it again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Doomhammer
magic.desc:
Long ago on the world of Draenor, an orc named Gelnar set out to fashion a weapon that would empower his people against their ogre foes. He forged a fearsome hammer in the heat of an elemental pool of lava. Dubbed Doomhammer, this weapon was passed down through generations of Blackrock orcs. An ancient prophecy foretold that possession of the hammer would someday leave the Blackrock lineage; this prophecy came true when Thrall, an orc shaman, proved himself the weapon's worthy wielder.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It deals an extra 1d8 Lightning damage on a hit.

Gelnar's Gifts. While holding Doomhammer, you gain the following benefits:

- Doom Winds. Your fury carries the unbridled momentum of a windstorm. While your Rage is active, your Speed is doubled, and you can take an extra Attack action (one attack only) on each of your turns.
- Lava Stride. You take no damage from molten lava and can walk across it as if it were solid ground.
- Lightning Rod. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you would take Lightning damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage to 0.
- Storm's Passage. You can cast Wind Walk from this weapon. Once the weapon has been used to cast this spell, it can't be used to cast it again until the next dawn.

Random Properties. Doomhammer has the following random properties:

- 2 minor beneficial properties
- 1 major beneficial property
- 1 minor detrimental property

Destroy

magic.name: Experimental Goblin Jetpack
magic.desc: While wearing this pack, you can take a Magic action to fire up its jets. The jets remain active for 1 hour or until you end the effect early as a Magic action. The jets give you a Fly Speed of 60 feet. If you are aloft when the jets become inactive, you fall. When the jets stop, you can't use them again for 1d12 hours.

magic.name: Figurine of Wondrous Power (Jeweled Panther)
magic.desc:
A Figurine of Wondrous Power is a statuette small enough to fit in a pocket. If you take a Magic action to throw the figurine to a point on the ground within 60 feet of yourself, the figurine becomes a living creature specified in the figurine's description below. If the space where the creature would appear is occupied by other creatures or objects, or if there isn't enough space for the creature, the figurine doesn't become a creature.

The creature is Friendly to you and your allies. It understands your languages, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your Initiative count. If you issue no commands, the creature defends itself but takes no other actions.

The creature exists for a duration specific to each figurine. At the end of the duration, the creature reverts to its figurine form. It reverts to a figurine early if its creature form drops to 0 Hit Points or if you take a Magic action while touching the creature to make it revert to figurine form. When the creature becomes a figurine again, its property can't be used again until a certain amount of time has passed, as specified below.

Jeweled Panther (Rare). This statuette is of a panther made from jade, onyx, ruby, sapphire, or sunstone. It can become a Large Panther with a Fly Speed of 30 feet for up to 12 hours and can be ridden as a mount. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed.

magic.name: Flask of the Titans
magic.desc:
When you drink this potion, your Hit Point maximum and current Hit Points increase by 30 for 1 hour.

The golden liquid in this flask tastes like honey and gleams with the light of dawn.

magic.name: Fragment of Frozen Bone
magic.desc: As a Magic action, you can use a command word to cause this tiny piece of bone from Lord Marrowgar's remains to transform into a miniature replica of Lord Marrowgar called Boneshard. Boneshard serves as an undead companion creature using the rules in D&D: World of Warcraft. It remains transformed until you use the command word to dismiss it, it takes any damage, or you summon another companion creature. Occasionally it shouts, "BONE STORM!" as it circles you on the ground.

magic.name: Frostmourne
magic.desc:
Runes of domination adorn this icy mourneblade. The Jailer—one of the rulers of the Shadowlands—originally sought to use Frostmourne to subjugate Azeroth, and that cruel intention forever lingers in the form of a prophecy: "Whosoever takes up this blade shall wield power eternal. Just as the blade rends flesh, so must power scar the spirit." Arthas Menethil was the first to discover the prophecy's true meaning when he lost his soul by wielding the sword, ultimately becoming the Lich King.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It deals an extra 2d12 Cold damage on a hit. Whenever you use Frostmourne to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, the creature dies, and its soul is trapped in the sword. The target can't be raised from the dead until Frostmourne is destroyed.

Pawn of the Lich King. While you're attuned to Frostmourne, the Lich King can see through your eyes, hear through your ears, and communicate with you telepathically over any distance, even across planes.

Prophecy of Frostmourne. When you attune to Frostmourne, your creature type becomes Undead, and your alignment becomes Neutral Evil. These changes remain even if your Attunement ends.

Twisted Aura. If you are a Paladin, you also gain the following benefits while attuned to Frostmourne:

- Marshal Undead. Undead creatures of your choice (excluding you) in your Aura of Protection have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws.
- Numb to Cold. Allies in you

magic.name: Gnomeregan Engineering Device
magic.desc:
Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Gnomeregan

You can request a complicated engineering device from the leaders of Gnomeregan before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive a mechanical device that functions as a Wand of Wonder, but it can't regain charges, and it explodes dramatically but harmlessly when its last charge is expended. The device doesn't require Attunement, but it functions only for you.

magic.name: Goblin Jumper Cables
magic.desc:
As a Magic action, you can attach these cables to a dead creature and attempt to return the creature to life. Make a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check using Tinker's Tools. On a successful check, the creature revives with 1 Hit Point as long as the creature has been dead no longer than 1 minute and didn't die of old age. On a failed check, you take 2d6 Lightning damage.

Once used, a set of Goblin Jumper Cables can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Hearthstone
magic.desc:
A Hearthstone teleports you to a predetermined location—usually an inn. Activating the stone takes 1 minute and a Magic action. You appear in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the destination you previously set.

While you are at an inn (or other locations at the DM's discretion), you can take a Magic action to set that location as the destination for your Hearthstone's teleportation. That location becomes your destination until you change it.

One Hearthstone doesn't count against the number of magic items you can have Attunement to.

magic.name: Helm of Domination
magic.desc:
This ornate helm is infused with the power of domination—a form of runic magic intended to utterly suppress the will of another being. The helm (along with its companion Artifact, Frostmourne) allowed its wearers—three successive Lich Kings—to rule the Scourge.

Attuning to the Helm. When you attune to the helm, make a DC 18 Charisma saving throw. On a successful save, you take 10d6 Psychic damage. On a failed save, your soul merges with the Lich King, who then takes control of your body like a puppet, and you become an NPC under the DM's control.

While attuned to the helm, you are unwilling to part with the helm, wearing it at all times, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to the helm.

Properties of the Helm. While attuned to the helm, your alignment is Neutral Evil, and you gain the following benefits:

- Command the Scourge. As a Magic action, you can send a psychic command to each Undead that is part of the Scourge. Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 20). On a successful check, you can issue a general command to the Undead Scourge, such as "attack any creature you come across" or "guard my stronghold," or you can issue a command to a specific member of the Scourge, such as "deliver a plague to Stormwind." Whether or not you succeed, this property of the helm can't be used again until the next dawn.
- Truesight. You have Truesight with a range of 120 feet.
- Spellcasting. The helm has 8 charges and regains 1d4 + 4 expended charges daily a

magic.name: Invincible's Reins
magic.desc:
These reins are a heavy metal chain attached to a bridle set with glowing blue crystals. The reins have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend 1 charge to cast Find Steed (level 5 version).

When you cast Find Steed from the reins, the summoned steed is Invincible, the mount of Arthas—an Undead horse with mummified flesh, glowing blue eyes, and batlike wings. The steed has the Undead type, deals Necrotic damage with its Otherworldly Slam attack, and has this Bonus Action:

Ghostly Stride (Undead Only; Recharges After a Long Rest). The steed and its rider can move through other creatures and objects this turn as if they were Difficult Terrain. Both steed and rider take 5 (1d10) Force damage if they end their turn inside an object.

Invincible is Neutral Evil and unshakably loyal to Arthas, the Lich King. Use the guidelines for conflict with sentient magic items in the Dungeon Master's Guide to determine what happens if Invincible's rider acts contrary to the mount's alignment or in opposition to the Lich King. Invincible can refuse the reins' summons in situations of conflict.

magic.name: Judgment Armor
magic.desc:
While wearing this armor, you are under the effects of the Detect Evil and Good and Protection from Evil and Good spells (no Concentration required). If you are a Paladin, the effects of Protection from Evil and Good extend to creatures of your choice in your Aura of Protection.

The wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

If the wearer has a Strength score lower than 15, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

magic.name: Life-Staff of the Web Lair
magic.desc:
This staff has 8 charges.

Arachnid's Grace. While attuned to the staff, you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and along ceilings without using your hands. You also gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed. You ignore movement restrictions caused by webs, and you know the location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

Web. While holding the staff, you can expend 1 charge to cast Web (save DC 18) from it.

Vampiric Silk. While holding the staff, you can take a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge to have a creature in the area of your Web spell make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. (The creature makes the save with Disadvantage if it has the Restrained condition from the webbing.) The creature takes 4d10 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Either way, you regain Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt.

Regaining Charges. The staff regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff dissolves into a swarm of harmless spiders and is destroyed.

Versatile. A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Mastery: Topple. If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a fai

magic.name: Light's Vengeance
magic.desc:
Light's Vengeance is the weapon Arthas Menethil wielded during his life as a paladin in service to the Order of the Silver Hand—before his corruption and transformation into the Lich King. An enormous and heavy hammer, its silver head etched with runes of power and its haft wrapped in blue leather, it carries the blessing of the Light. Arthas discarded the weapon when he took up Frostmourne.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this weapon, and it deals an extra 2d10 Radiant damage to Undead.

Repel Undead. While holding the weapon, you can take the Magic action to cause brilliant light to burst around you in a 30-foot Emanation. Each Undead in the Emanation makes a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 4d8 Radiant damage and has the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions for 1 minute. While Frightened, a target must use its movement on each of its turns to move as far from you as it can. This effect ends early on a target if it takes any damage.

Random Properties. Though Light's Vengeance was blessed by the Light and wielded by the Light's champion, the weapon carries the stain of the Lich King's corruption. The weapon has the following random properties:

- 2 minor beneficial properties
- 1 major beneficial property
- 2 minor detrimental properties

Destroying the Weapon. Striking Light's Vengeance with Frostmourne destroys the maul.

Heavy. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a M

magic.name: Noggenfogger Elixir
magic.desc:
Noggenfogger Elixir is an unpredictable potion invented by Marin Noggenfogger, the trade prince of the Steamwheedle Cartel. It is highly coveted by adventurers (particularly goblins), despite or perhaps because of its unpredictable effects. When you drink this potion, roll 1d6: On a 1-2, you take on a skeletal appearance for 1d4 hours, during which time you don't need to breathe. (Not breathing doesn't give you Exhaustion levels.) On a 3-4, you gain the Reduce effect of the Enlarge/Reduce spell for 1d4 hours (no Concentration required). On a 5-6, your rate of descent while falling slows to 60 feet per round for 10 minutes. During that time, you take no damage from falling.

Drinking multiple Noggenfogger Elixirs doesn't require you to roll on the Potion Miscibility table in the Dungeon Master's Guide.

This green potion is oily in the mouth.

magic.name: Philosopher's Stone
magic.desc:
A Philosopher's Stone is a powerful reagent used in alchemy, and it can be effectively used only by the alchemist who created it. While you carry it, you gain the following benefits.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use your Philosopher's Stone as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

Transmute Resources. If you spend 1 hour (which can be concurrent with a Short Rest) with your Philosopher's Stone and crafting resources of a single kind (fish, gems, herbs, ores or stones, leather or hide, or cloth), you can magically transmute the resources into resources of a different kind but the same value. Thus, you can convert 100 GP worth of herbs into 100 GP worth of ore or vice versa, or change 500 GP of mithril (a common ore) into 500 GP of truesilver (a rare ore).

Mixology. When you roll a die to determine the effect of a potion you drink (including the result of mixing potions), you can roll the die twice and choose either result. If a potion you drink has a duration, that duration is doubled.

magic.name: Potions of Mana
magic.desc:
You regain one expended spell slot when you drink this potion. The level of the spell slot depends on the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below. (When a level range is presented, you choose the spell slot you regain.)

Whatever its potency, the potion's blue liquid glows with an inner light.

| Potion                      | Spell Slot Level |  Rarity  |
|-----------------------------|:----------------:|:--------:|
| Potion of Mana            |         1        |  Common  |
| Potion of Mana (Greater)  |        1-3       | Uncommon |
| Potion of Mana (Superior) |        1-5       |   Rare   |

magic.name: Potions of Rejuvenation
magic.desc:
You regain Hit Points and one expended spell slot when you drink this potion. The number of Hit Points and the level of the spell slot depend on the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below. (When a level range is presented, you choose the spell slot you regain.)

Whatever its potency, the potion's magenta liquid glows faintly from within.

| Potion                              |  HP and Spell Slot Regained |   Rarity  |
|-------------------------------------|:---------------------------:|:---------:|
| Potion of Rejuvenation            |  3d4 + 3 HP; Slot level: 1  |  Uncommon |
| Potion of Rejuvenation (Greater)  | 6d4 + 6 HP; Slot level: 1-3 |    Rare   |
| Potion of Rejuvenation (Superior) | 9d4 + 9 HP; Slot level: 1-5 | Very Rare |

magic.name: Ring of Maddening Whispers
magic.desc:
This ring resembles a fleshy purple tentacle banded with dark metal and suffused with a reddish glow. While wearing it, you can cast Dominate Monster (level 9 version) from it (spell save DC 19). Once you do, you can't use the ring to do so again until the next dawn.

Whenever a creature makes a successful saving throw against the spell cast from the ring, you take 5d10 Psychic damage and have the Incapacitated condition until the end of your next turn, as a chorus of babbling whispers assails your mind.

magic.name: Rod of the Sleepwalker
magic.desc:
This rod puts creatures into a suggestible, sleepwalking state. You can cast Dominate Monster (save DC 17) from this rod, with the following modifications:

Duration. The spell's duration is Concentration, up to 8 hours.

Immunity. Creatures that don't sleep, such as elves, or that have Immunity to the Exhaustion condition automatically succeed on the save.

Memory. An affected creature remembers nothing from the spell's duration once the spell ends.

Once the rod has been used to cast the spell in this way, it can't be used to do so again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Shadow's Edge
magic.desc:
Highlord Darion Mograine of the Knights of the Ebon Blade forged Shadow's Edge in his runeforge, combining the holy power of Light's Vengeance with primordial saronite—the blood of the Old God Yogg-Saron in mineral form—and the toxic venom from two of the Lich King's minions. The result is a mighty axe with the potential, ultimately, to destroy the Lich King.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this weapon.

Drain Soul. Whenever you use Shadow's Edge to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, the axe slays the creature and devours its soul unless it is a Construct. A creature whose soul has been devoured by Shadow's Edge can be restored to life only by a Wish spell.

When Shadow's Edge devours a soul, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to half the slain creature's Hit Point maximum (round down).

Random Properties. The weapon has the following random properties:

- 1 minor beneficial property
- 1 minor detrimental property

Unholy Infusion. Once Shadow's Edge has been infused with Professor Putricide's mutated slime, it gains the following additional random properties:

- 1 minor beneficial property
- 1 major detrimental property

In addition, when you hit a creature with Shadow's Edge, you can cast Blight (save DC 19) from it on the target as a Bonus Action. Once you use the weapon to cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

Blood Infusion. Once Shadow's Edge has been infused with blood from Lana'thel's Blo

magic.name: Shadowfang
magic.desc:
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Mark of the Worgen. In most circumstances, the weapon appears unremarkable. But under the night sky, ragged fur and sharp fangs sprout around the sword's cross guard. While transformed in this way, Shadowfang deals an extra 2d6 Necrotic damage on a hit. The weapon returns to normal at dawn or if it is brought indoors.

Versatile. A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Mastery: Sap. If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

magic.name: Shadowmourne
magic.desc:
Highlord Darion Mograine transformed Shadow's Edge into Shadowmourne after the weapon had been infused with unholy power, blood magic, and undying frost, along with shadowfrost shards from the Frozen Throne.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this weapon.

Soul Fragments. When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using Shadowmourne, the creature takes an extra 1d12 Necrotic damage, and you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage taken.

Drain Soul. Whenever you use Shadowmourne to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, the axe slays the creature and devours its soul unless it is a Construct. A creature whose soul has been devoured by Shadowmourne can be restored to life only by a Wish spell.

When Shadowmourne devours a soul, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the slain creature's Hit Point maximum.

Chaos Bane. If you have at least 12 Temporary Hit Points, you can take a Bonus Action to sacrifice all your Temporary Hit Points. Each creature of your choice in a 15-foot Emanation originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 21), taking damage equal to the Temporary Hit Points you sacrificed on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Until the end of your next turn, you have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws.

Random Properties. The weapon has the same random properties it had in its final stage as Shadow's Edge:

- 2 minor beneficial properties
- 2 major beneficial proper

magic.name: Shalamayne
magic.desc:
When dragon magic split King Varian Wrynn into two versions of himself, one of his selves wielded the night elven blade Shalla'tor, while the other wielded the night elven blade Ellemayne. Varian eventually merged his twin selves back into one whole. In doing so, he inadvertently fused the blades into a new weapon called Shalamayne.

The Jailer, one of the rulers of the Shadowlands, once stole and reforged Shalamayne into a mourneblade called Kingsmourne. But Varian's son, Anduin Wrynn, later restored Shalamayne to its rightful form. Anduin is the sword's last known wielder.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It deals an extra 2d12 Force damage on a hit.

Dual Mastery. If you have the Weapon Mastery feature and choose Greatsword as one of your mastered weapons, you can use both the Graze and Sap mastery properties at once while wielding Shalamayne.

Splitting and Reuniting the Sword. While holding Shalamayne, you can take a Magic action to end your Attunement to the weapon and split it into two magic swords: Shalla'tor and Ellemayne. Each is a +3 Longsword with the Finesse and Light properties. A creature who holds both swords can take a Magic action to rejoin them into Shalamayne, attuning to the weapon instantly.

Random Properties. Shalamayne has the following random properties:

- 2 minor beneficial properties
- 1 major beneficial property

Destroying Shalamayne. One can destroy Shalamayne by splitting it into

magic.name: Staff of Light and Shadow
magic.desc:
This staff has two forms: a shadowy state known as Anathema and a holy state known as Benediction. While attuned to the staff, you can switch the staff from one state to the other at dawn.

Anathema. As Anathema, the staff grants the following benefits:

- Necrotic Resistance. While attuned to the staff, you have Resistance to Necrotic damage.
- Shadow Mana. While you're holding the staff, when you cast a level 1-5 spell from the Necromancy school that would expend a spell slot, you can roll 1d6. If the number on the die exceeds the spell's level, the spell slot isn't expended.

Benediction. As Benediction, the staff grants the following benefits:

- Radiant Resistance. While attuned to the staff, you have Resistance to Radiant Damage.
- Light-Blessed Healing. While you're holding the staff, when you cast a spell that would restore Hit Points to a creature, you can treat the spell as if it had been cast using a spell slot of 1 level higher.

Versatile. A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Mastery: Topple. If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

magic.name: Steamwheedle Apparatus
magic.desc:
This item first appears to be a sealed iron barrel weighing 500 pounds. The barrel has a hidden catch, which can be found with a successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check. Releasing the catch unlocks a hatch at one end of the barrel, allowing two Medium or smaller creatures to crawl inside. Ten levers are set in a row at the far end, each in a neutral position, able to move up or down. When certain levers are used, the apparatus transforms to resemble a giant lobster.

The Steamwheedle Apparatus is a Large object with the following statistics: AC 20; HP 200; Speed 30 ft., Swim 30 ft. (or 0 ft. for both if the legs aren't extended); Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage.

To be used as a vehicle, the apparatus requires one pilot. While the apparatus's hatch is closed, the compartment is airtight and watertight. The compartment holds enough air for 10 hours of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.

The apparatus floats on water. It can also go underwater to a depth of 900 feet. Below that, the vehicle takes 2d6 Bludgeoning damage each minute from pressure.

A creature in the compartment can take a Utilize action to move as many as two of the apparatus's levers up or down. After each use, a lever goes back to its neutral position. Each lever, from left to right, functions as shown in the Steamwheedle Apparatus Levers table.

Steamwheedle Apparatus Levers

| Lever | Up

magic.name: Sulfuras, Hand of Ragnaros
magic.desc:
The elementium Maul Sulfuras is the weapon of Ragnaros, the Elemental Lord of Fire. In the beginning, the four elemental lords warred against one another for dominance over the nascent Azeroth. While the other elemental lords fought with mastery of their own elements, Ragnaros used Sulfuras to turn their elements against them, boiling seas, choking the skies with smoke and embers, and turning mountains into erupting volcanoes.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. A creature hit by this weapon takes an extra 1d10 Fire damage and starts burning, taking 1d10 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns instead of the normal burning damage.

Ignite the Elements. While holding this weapon, you can take a Magic action to produce one of the following effects. Once an effect has been used, that effect can't be used again until the next dawn:

- Boiling Point. You cause any container or body of water within 1 mile of you to boil for 1 minute. A creature that enters the boiling water or starts its turn there takes 2d10 Fire damage.
- Embersmoke. You cast Incendiary Cloud (save DC 18) from the weapon.
- Eruption. You make lava erupt in a 10-foot-radius, 60-foot-high Cylinder centered on a point on the ground you can see within 120 feet. Each creature in that area makes a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 9d10 Fire damage plus 9d10 Bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Random Proper

magic.name: Sundial of Eternal Dusk
magic.desc:
Despite its name, a Sundial of Eternal Dusk resembles a lantern more than a sundial. A rough shard of green saronite metal hangs suspended above an iron cylinder, flanked by wings sculpted from brass. Glowing green gas billows between the saronite shard and the cylinder, and a smaller green shard bobs between two forked prongs on the bottom of the implement. A curved handle above the larger shard allows the item to be held easily in one hand. While you hold the sundial, you know what time it is.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use the sundial as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

Cloak of Shadows. The sundial emits shadow that fills your space with Dim Light, making the space Lightly Obscured and giving you Resistance to Radiant damage. The shadow doesn't obscure your vision.

Spells. The sundial has 20 charges and regains 1d6 + 3 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the sundial, you can cast one of the spells on the following table from it (save DC 19). The table indicates how many charges you must expend to cast the spell.

| Spell                                                               | Charge Cost |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------:|
| Darkness                                                          |           2 |
| Dimension Door (the destination must be in Dim Light or Darkness) |           4 |
| Evard's Black Tentacles                                           |           4 |
| Fear

magic.name: Thrice Fanged Signet
magic.desc:
This silver ring is adorned with a pyramid shape topped with a glowing blue crystal. The three fangs that give it its name protrude from the underside of the pyramid to pierce the wearer's finger.

When you cast a spell while wearing this ring, you can let the ring draw your blood to empower the spell. If you do, your current and maximum Hit Points are reduced by 3d6, and the spell's effects are determined as if you had used a spell slot 1 level higher than the slot you used (maximum level 9).

magic.name: Tiny Abomination in a Jar
magic.desc:
When you roll an 11 on the d20 for an attack roll while this monstrous item is on your person, you gain a Mote of Anger—a Tiny, invulnerable mote of glowing red light that orbits your head at a distance of 1d3 feet. A Mote of Anger lasts until you finish a Long Rest. Each Mote of Anger gives you a +2 bonus to damage rolls.

If you ever have four Motes of Anger at once, they erupt and fill you with rage, allowing you to make an immediate weapon attack with Advantage on the attack roll. The Motes of Anger grant their damage bonuses to this attack if they hit, and they dissipate after the attack whether it hits or misses.

The tiny abomination floating in this jar appears lifeless, but if you have one or more Motes of Anger, it stirs, growing increasingly animated the more Motes of Anger you have.

magic.name: Troll's Blood Elixir
magic.desc:
When you drink this potion, you regain 2 Hit Points. At the start of each of your turns for the next 1 minute, you regain that number of Hit Points again if you have at least 1 Hit Point. This thick green elixir is made from herbs.

No trolls were harmed in the making of this elixir.

magic.name: Corrupted Ashbringer
magic.desc:
Infused with the Holy Light and forged by King Magni Bronzebeard on the Great Anvil of Ironforge, Ashbringer was once the pride and joy of the knightly Mograine family. But when the traitorous Renault Mograine used the sword to kill his father, it became corrupted. The sword was claimed by the Scourge until Renault's brother, Darion Mograine, betrayed the Lich King and delivered the weapon to Tirion Fordring—an act of heroism that cleansed Ashbringer of its corruption and restored the sword to its rightful form.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It deals an extra 1d10 Fire damage on a hit, or an extra 3d10 Fire damage if the target is Undead.

Changing States. When first encountered, Ashbringer is in either its True State or its Corrupted State. At the DM's discretion, Ashbringer changes into its Corrupted State if its wielder uses it to commit an act of legendary wickedness; it changes into its True State if its wielder uses it to commit an act of legendary heroism. Ashbringer's current state grants you one of the following benefits:

Steal Life (Corrupted State Only). Whenever you use Ashbringer to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you gain 20 Temporary Hit Points.

Sentience. Ashbringer is a sentient weapon with an Intelligence of 14, a Wisdom of 17, and a Charisma of 17. It is Lawful Evil in its Corrupted State. It has hearing and Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.

The weapon communicates telepathically wi

magic.name: Heward's Hireling Armor
magic.desc:
A number of Kwalish's experiments were attempts to research the works of the legendary mage Heward, who first crafted what he named hireling armor. While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC. In addition, the armor's animated straps can assist with the drawing and sheathing of weapons, such that you can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.

This armor also has six pockets, each of which is an extradimensional space. Each pocket can hold up to 20 pounds of material, not exceeding a volume of 2 cubic feet. The armor always weighs 10 pounds, regardless of its pockets' contents. Placing an object into one of the armor's pockets follows the normal rules for interacting with objects. Retrieving an item from a pocket of the armor requires you to use an action. When you reach into a pocket for a specific item, the item is always magically on top.

Placing the armor inside an extradimensional space created by a bag of holding, a Heward's handy haversack, or a similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

magic.name: Leather Golem Armor
magic.desc:
Strange rituals have repurposed the body of a flesh golem into this partially sentient suit of leather armor. While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC and to saving throws against spells and other magical effects. In addition, you gain the following properties:

Immutable Form. You are immune to any spell or effect that would alter your form.

Lightning Absorption. You gain resistance to lightning damage. Whenever you take lightning damage, you gain 5 temporary hit points.

Curse. This armor is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with a remove curse spell or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the armor. In addition, while you wear the cursed armor, you gain the following properties:

Aversion of Fire. If you take fire damage, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of your next turn.

Berserk. Whenever a critical hit is made against you, roll a d6. On a 6, the armor causes you to go berserk. On each of your turns while berserk, you attack the nearest creature you can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, you attack an object, with preference for an object smaller than yourself. Once the armor causes you to go berserk, it cannot be removed. You continue to attack until you are incapacitated or until another creature is able to calm you with appropriate magic (such as a calm emotions spell) or a successful DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check.

magic.name: Nightbringer
magic.desc:
This heavy mace has a dark oaken handle and a head of blackened steel trimmed with gold. In combat, the mace's head is wreathed in inky black energy.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon. When you hit with an attack roll using it, the target takes an additional 4d4 radiant damage.

If you have an evil alignment, you also gain the following benefits when attuned to Nightbringer:

Blessing of the Dragon Queen. You are immune to the charmed and frightened conditions, and you gain immunity to one of the following damage types (choose when you attune to the weapon): acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison.

Eyes of Midnight. You have darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.

Midnight Shroud. The weapon has 6 charges. When you hit a creature with an attack using this weapon, you can expend one charge to force the creature to make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is blinded until the start of your next turn. The weapon regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn.

magic.name: Niko's Mace
magic.desc:
This Mace has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Mace, you can expend 1 of its charges to cast Summon Celestial (+9 to hit with spell attacks).

Mastery: Sap. If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

magic.name: Powered Armor (LLK)
magic.desc:
Powered armor resembles a suit of unusual plate armor, with finely articulated joints connected by an oily, black, leather-like material. The armor has been worked to create the appearance of a heavily muscled warrior, and its great helm is unusual in that it has no openings—only a broad glass plate in the front with a second piece of glass above it. Strange plates, tubing, and large metal bosses adorn the armor in seemingly random fashion. On the back of the armor's left gauntlet is a rectangular metal box, from which projects a short rod tipped with a cone-shaped red crystal.

While wearing this armor, you gain the following benefits:

- You have a +1 bonus to AC.Your Strength score is 18 (this has no effect if your Strength is already 18 or higher)
- You have advantage on death saving throws.
- The armor has further capabilities that can be powered either by energy cells or by your own life energy. You can use a bonus action to draw power from an energy cell or sacrifice hit points to gain one of the following benefits:

- Emit a force field to gain 2d6 + 5 temporary hit points (1 charge or 5 hit points)
- Activate boosters to gain a flying speed of 15 feet for 1 minute (1 charge or 5 hit points)
- Fire arm-mounted laser: Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, range 120 feet, one target. Hit: 2d6 radiant damage (1 charge or 5 hit points)
- Translate any writing you can see in any nonmagical language, to a total of one thousand words over 1 minute (1 charge or 5 hit points)
- Fil

magic.name: Ruinblade
magic.desc:
Ruinblade is a unique weapon possessed by Moghadam, the architect of the Tomb of Horrors. A symbol of his authority, Moghadam carries the weapon during the time frame of the adventure to intimidate the tomb's workers. (In later years, after Acererak trapped Moghadam in the completed tomb as an undead archwraith, Moghadam was able to use the weapon as his own phylactery.)

A small jade version of the green devil face of the Tomb of Horrors is fashioned into the hilt of the weapon, with the blade extending from its open mouth. The blade always appears ruined and rusting, and causes its surroundings to appear reflected in the blade as if in a state of decay.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit an undead creature with it, the attack deals an extra 1d8 force damage.

In addition, the weapon has the following properties:

Blighted Ruin. You can cast the blight spell from the weapon (DC 15). Once used, this property of the weapon can't be used until the next dawn.

Destructive Ruin. You can cast the disintegrate spell from the weapon, but can target only a nonmagical object or a creation of magical force. Once used, this property of the weapon can't be used until dawn seven days later.

Curse. This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with a remove curse spell or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the weapon.

The weapon must take direct part in the destructio

magic.name: Twin Blades of Azzinoth
magic.desc:
This pair of demonic warglaives once belonged to Azzinoth, an ancient doomguard commander of the Burning Legion. Illidan Stormrage slew Azzinoth millennia ago during the War of the Ancients and reforged the blades for himself, allowing him to use fel magic against the demons of the Legion.

Magic Weapons. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with these magic weapons. Each deals an extra 2d8 Psychic damage if the target is a Fiend; this Psychic damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.

Fel Synchronization. If you hit the same creature with both weapons on a turn, that creature makes a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw immediately after the second weapon hits. On a failed save, the creature is racked by fel magic and has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn.

Flames of Azzinoth. As a Magic action, you can throw one of the weapons to an unoccupied space on the ground you can see within 30 feet of you. The blade transforms into a fiery green fiend as if you had cast the Summon Fiend spell (choose the Devil option). The spell lasts for 1 minute, and when the summoned fiend disappears, the weapon reappears in your hand. You can't turn that weapon into a Fiend again until 7 days have passed.

Random Properties. The Twin Blades of Azzinoth have the following random properties:

1 minor beneficial property1 major beneficial property1 minor detrimental property Destroying the Blades. Reciting an ancient poem called "Gift of the Light" over the blades causes

magic.name: Trident of Henchantment
magic.desc:
A jasper effigy of a chicken's head rests at the top of this trident, and an egg-shaped amethyst is fixed to its base. It is a strange weapon, but is highly coveted by farmers and livestock owners.

This magic weapon has 4 charges, and regains 1d4 expended charges at dawn. When you use the Attack action with this weapon, you can immediately expend 1 of its charges to cast the Polymorph spell (save DC 15) and transform your target into a hen (AC 10, HP 1, Speed 30 ft) for 1 hour. The illusion appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 ft of you. You can take an Attack or Magic action on your turn to attack or cast a spell as if you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses. magic.desc:
This punch knife style weapon is carved from a single chunk of superconductive dark violet metal that binds to the fist and forearm with black leather straps.

When you score a Critical Hit against a creature with this magic weapon, that creature takes an extra 2d6 Lightning damage. Additionally, while you are attuned to this magical weapon, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and you can cast Jump on yourself.

Mastery: Sap. If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

magic.name: Ratbite
magic.desc:
These pungent weapons are made of leather of dubious origin with clumps of fur still attached. The leather grip fits snugly over the knuckles, with rat teeth and bits of bone sticking out the outward facing side. It gives off an unpleasant odor.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with these magic weapons. While you are attuned to these weapons, you have Immunity to magical contagions. Any creature who takes damage from this Constitution saving throw or contract Sewer Plague. When you score a Critical Hit against a creature with these magic weapons, it takes an extra 2d4 Necrotic damage and has Disadvantage on saving throws against magical contagions for seven days.

magic.name: Mithril Mail-shirt
magic.desc:
Craftsmanship: Dwarven

A Mithril mail-shirt is half its normal weight, and can be worn under normal clothes. When you are wearing it, your base Armour Class is 14 + your Dexterity modifier (max 4), and you are considered proficient with it if you have proficiency with light armour.

magic.name: Angelskin Armor
magic.desc:
This leather armor is made from the flayed flesh of angels.

While attuned to the armor, you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Any Celestial that sees this armor immediately becomes Hostiles toward the wearer, and any Fiend wants to possess it at any cost.

magic.name: Ardor
magic.desc:
The blades of this axe smolder with an inner light, and the dark wooden handle is accented with silver. After the celestial realm turned back yet another assault from the forces of evil, a fiendish forge master received a vision, allowing them to craft a weapon like no other. Ardor now lies in a hidden vault, waiting to be wielded by a scion of darkness who strikes on behalf of the forces of the Arch Daemons.

The fiends don't realize that an equally powerful weapon rests in the hands of the celestials, who wage eternal war against them. In the interest of maintaining order, the fates who inspired the forgemaster to craft Ardor also sent a similar vision to a smith of heaven.

Axe of Hell. This magic battleaxe grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. When you hit with it, the target takes an extra 2d10 Necrotic damage.

Champion of Evil. While holding the battleaxe, you have Immunity to the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned conditions.

Ardor's Pursuit. Ardor's Pursuit: You can take a Bonus Action to toss the axe into the air, causing it to hover magically in your space. While the weapon hovers, you can take a Bonus Action to cause it to fly up to 50 feet to another spot within 50 feet of you. As part of the same Bonus Action, you can either grasp the weapon if it is within reach, or cause it to attack one creature within 5 feet of the weapon. The weapon uses your attack roll and adds your ability modifier to the damage rolls. The weapon ceases to

magic.name: Armor of Zombie Flesh
magic.desc:
This armor is formed from the tanned flesh of a zombie.

While wearing this armor, your Armor Class becomes 14 + your Dexterity modifier. While attuned to this armor, when you take Necrotic damage, you can use a Reaction to halve that Necrotic damage (round down).

magic.name: Bow of Four
magic.desc:
This white wooden bow is set with four gemstones: a ruby, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.

When you hold this bow, as a Bonus Action you can summon a magical arrow composed of one of the four elements. You must still make an attack roll to hit a creature with the magical arrow, and it does only the damage listed.

When you take the Attack action, you can attack with this summoned arrow. If you have a feature that lets you fire more than one arrow on a turn, you can fire other arrows as part of the Attack action.

Each time you summon a magical arrow, you must choose one of the four options below. If you do not fire the arrow within 1 minute of summoning it, it dissolves.

Arrow of Air. On a hit, the arrow of air deals 4d8 Lightning damage.

Arrow of Earth. On a hit, the arrow of earth deals 4d8 Bludgeoning damage.

Arrow of Fire. On a hit, the arrow of fire deals 4d8 Fire damage.

Arrow of Water. On a hit, the arrow of water deals 4d8 Cold damage.

magic.desc:
This armor, fashioned from the body of an Empyrean brazen bull, gleams brightly in direct sunlight. While wearing this armor, you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class. In addition, you have Resistance to Fire and Radiant damage.

The wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

If the wearer has a Strength score lower than 15, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

magic.desc:

The wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

This strange weapon is fashioned from the mandible of a hivewolf. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon. When you roll a 19 or 20 on your attack roll with this weapon, that attack does an additional 2d6 Acid damage. In addition, you have Immunity to Acid damage while wielding the weapon.

magic.desc:
This floor-length leather duster is the color of dying embers. You have a +2 bonus to Armor Class while wearing this armor.

The coat has 3 charges. When you hit a creature with a melee attack, and that creature is not at its Hit Point maximum, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra 1d10 Fire damage to the target. The coat regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

magic.name: Coldrazor (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This infamous axe is wielded by the memori lich known as Runa Banasár. It appears to be made of ice, carved with runes and studded with various tiny, glittering gems.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra 4d6 Cold damage. If a single attack with Coldrazor deals more than 20 points of Cold damage, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn.

Immediately after hitting or missing with a ranged attack made with this weapon, it flies back to your hand.

magic.desc:
This shimmering breastplate is forged from a giant dragonfly's carapace and adorned with a cape of gossamer fabric. You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while you wear this armor.

While wearing this armor, you can take an action to transform the cape into dragonfly wings for 1 hour. While this effect lasts, you have a Fly Speed of 30 feet.

If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Fey Transformation, the armor's effect lasts for 2 hours, during which time you have a Fly Speed of 60 feet.

Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Light Drinker
magic.desc:
This sword's hilt and blade are forged from a single piece of black metal that absorbs the light around it. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Cold damage instead of Slashing damage. While attuned to the sword, you gain darkvision to 60 feet and can see in magical darkness.

As a Bonus Action, you can cause the sword to emit magical darkness in a 20-foot radius, and illumination is limited to Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

While the darkness is active, you can use an action to expand or reduce its radius of darkness by 5 feet each, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet each. You can use this feature again at the end of a Short, or Long Rest.

magic.desc:
This net is made of wire and thread from a suture golem. It can be used in the same manner as a normal Net, but once it restrains a target it coils and twists as if alive. Escaping the Living Net requires a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.

The Living Net has AC 15 and 15 HP. If destroyed, the net repairs itself after 1 minute.
