magic.name: Mummy Rot Antidote
magic.desc: White dust swirls constantly within this pale gray potion. When you drink the potion, it cures you of mummy rot.

magic.name: Pirate's Cutlass
magic.desc: This +1 shortsword is a terrifying weapon with a serrated edge. It grants its wielder advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks when brandished.

magic.name: Potion of Mana
magic.desc:
You regain one expended level 1 spell slot when you drink this potion.

The potion's blue liquid glows with an inner light.

magic.name: Potion of Rejuvenation
magic.desc:
You regain 3d4 + 3 Hit Points and one expended level 1 spell slot when you drink this potion.

The potion's magenta liquid glows faintly from within.

magic.name: Primal Amulet
magic.desc: This beaded jade necklace bears an ancient symbol of the River Heralds. When worn, the primal amulet allows its wearer to cast speak with animals, locate object, and pass without trace. Once the amulet has been used to cast a spell, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Prismatic Well
magic.desc: This well enhances the colors of the city of Harmony and invigorates the population. When the well is at full power, all good-aligned creatures that see the colors experience feelings of happiness and have advantage on all Charisma checks.

magic.name: Prying Blade
magic.desc: A hooked blade useful on board a ship or as a cutting tool in the wilderness, this +1 shortsword grants its wielder advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to climb or to escape while restrained.

magic.name: Sorcerous Spyglass
magic.desc: This elegant brass spyglass features an intricate lens mechanism. A creature looking through the sorcerous spyglass has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to detect things that can be seen. In addition, the user can view magical auras while looking through the spyglass, as if under the effect of a detect magic spell.

magic.name: The Infernal Machine of Lum the Mad
magic.desc:
This strange device was once thought to have been built by gods long forgotten and to have survived the eons since their passing, for it is incredibly ancient and crafted by means unlike anything known today. However, its true origins derive from a planar craft that crashed in the Barrier Peaks, for the Infernal Machine once functioned as this craft's central command console.

Explorers who discovered the crash site removed the command console and brought it back to civilization, not understanding its true purpose or powers. In later years, the console came into the possession of Baron Lum. By experimenting with its many controls, he was able to achieve astounding and destructive magical effects in the building of his empire, and so the artifact came to be known as the Infernal Machine of Lum the Mad. Yet with Lum's eventual defeat, his great machine was destroyed.

The Infernal Machine is a delicate, intricate, bulky, and heavy device, weighing some 5,500 pounds. It can be operated using a control panel containing sixty levers, forty dials, twenty switches, and a number of jeweled components. These controls generate all kinds of powers and effects, as noted below.

Silver Wire. The Infernal Machine's great size makes it largely immobile. To make ongoing use of the machine (such as while adventuring), it can be connected to its attuned user by a silver wire, a supply of which can always be produced from the machine's inner workings. This silver wire shares the same general na

magic.name: Thessaltoxin Antidote
magic.desc: This potion appears to change color and texture each time you look at it. When you drink the potion, it ends the polymorph effect imposed by thessaltoxin.

magic.name: Vanquisher's Banner
magic.desc: This battle-worn but unbroken standard bears the insignia of one of the forces of the Legion of Dusk. A creature that holds the vanquisher's banner can use a bonus action to grant an ally advantage on the ally's next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check.

magic.name: Vial of Thought Capture
magic.desc:
This dark blue vial allows you to read another's surface thoughts and capture them as thought strands, storing the strands within the vial. As an action, you can activate the vial to target a creature you can see within 10 feet of you to learn its surface thoughts and pull the thoughts learned out of the creature's head as a tangible glowing string of energy known as a thought strand. The strands can be stored in the vial for up to 24 hours or until the vial reaches capacity, in which case the oldest strands dissipate. A creature affected by the vial knows that its thoughts are being probed.

The vial can also store thought strands created by the encode thoughts cantrip. It does not extend the duration of those strands beyond 8 hours, but stored strands do not disappear if you cast encode thoughts again during the duration of the cantrip.

The vial has 3 charges and can store up to 3 thought strands. It regains all its charges daily at dusk.

magic.name: Vithrak, Gaze of the Deadman
magic.desc: This ring has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can take a Magic action and expend 1 charge to learn the Resistances, Vulnerabilities, and Immunities (if any) of a creature you can see within 120 feet of yourself. When you use this effect, your eyes briefly become glassy, gray husks.

magic.name: Whistle-Stick
magic.desc:
The grung of One Grung Above are trained to use this new musical instrument. This is a hollow tube with holes cut throughout, much like a flute. You can play music with it for entertainment, but the grung also swing it about by a sturdy cord (attached) to create a sound recognizable by other grung, so they know each other's approximate location. Additionally, grung that know Thieves' Cant can use a whistle stick in this manner to communicate over distance.

Instrument. If you have proficiency with a given musical instrument, you can add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to play music with the instrument. A bard can use a musical instrument as a spellcasting focus. Each type of musical instrument requires a separate proficiency.

See the Tool Proficiencies entry for more information.

Proficiency with a musical instrument indicates you are familiar with the techniques used to play it. You also have knowledge of some songs commonly performed with that instrument.

History. Your expertise aids you in recalling lore related to your instrument.

Performance. Your ability to put on a good show is improved when you incorporate an instrument into your act.

Compose a Tune. As part of a long rest, you can compose a new tune and lyrics for your instrument. You might use this ability to impress a noble or spread scandalous rumors with a catchy tune.

Musical InstrumentActivityDCIdentify a tune10Improvise a tune20

magic.name: Troll's Blood Elixirs
magic.desc:
When you drink this potion, you regain a number of Hit Points depending on the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below. At the start of each of your turns for the next 1 minute, you regain that number of Hit Points again if you have at least 1 Hit Point.

This thick green elixir is made from herbs. No trolls were harmed in the making of this elixir.

magic.name: Shard of the Kalt Rune
magic.desc:
This long, slender shard of ice is roughly the size of a dagger. The kalt rune—the rune of ice—glows within the shard. When first grasped, the shard emits a painful cold that leaves your hand and arm numb. That feeling passes after a moment, allowing the shard to be handled normally.

Frigid Touch (Simple Property). As an action, you scribe the kalt rune on the surface of any volume of water. The water freezes in a 10-foot radius around the spot where you scribed the rune.

Frost Friend (Simple Property). While you are attuned to this rune, you have resistance to fire damage.

Icy Mantle (Simple Property). As an action, you scribe the kalt rune using water onto yourself or another creature. The water instantly freezes into a mantle of protective ice that does not hinder movement or action. The next time the creature takes bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage, that damage is reduced to zero and the icy mantle is destroyed.

Freezing Bolt (Complex Property). As an action, you scribe this rune using water onto a creature within your reach as you expend a spell slot. The rune freezes in place, and the creature must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 12 + the level of the expended spell slot). On a failure, the creature takes 2d8 cold damage plus 1d8 cold damage per level of the expended spell slot, and its speed is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn. On a successful saving throw, the creature takes half as much damage and its speed is not affected.

Ice Brand (Co

magic.name: Bag of Bounty
magic.desc:
This is a sturdy leather sack with tiny Siberys shards embedded into the lining. If you have the Mark of Hospitality you can use an action to cast create food and water, drawing a feast from within the bag. You shape this meal with your thoughts. You can create the standard bland fare without requiring any sort of check, but you can attempt to create finer food by making a Charisma check; if you're proficient with cook's utensils, add your bonus to this check. A failed check results in a sour and squalid meal.

Food QualityDifficultyPoorNo roll requiredModest10Comfortable13Wealthy15Aristocratic18A bag of bounty can be used up to three times over the course of a day. After that, the bag can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Band of Loyalty
magic.desc: If you are reduced to zero hit points while attuned to a band of loyalty, you instantly die. These rings are favored by spies who can't afford to fall into enemy hands.

magic.name: Rings of Shared Suffering
magic.desc: These rings come in linked pairs. If you possess the Mark of Sentinel, you can use a bonus action to form a link to the creature attuned to the other ring; from then on, whenever that creature suffers damage, they only suffer half of that damage and you take the rest. This effect continues until you end it as a bonus action or until you or the other creature removes their ring. This effect isn't limited by range. A creature cannot be attuned to more than one ring of shared suffering.

magic.name: Imbued Wood (Quori Beech)
magic.desc:
Powerful manifest zones can infuse local trees with planar energies. A gifted artificer can tap into this to create a wand, staff, or rod that is especially effective at channeling a particular type of energy.

When you cast a spell that deals psychic damage, the spell gains a +1 bonus to one psychic damage roll of that spell.

magic.name: Quori Celestine Crystal
magic.desc:
An orb of shielding is made from crystal or stone aligned to one of the planes. While you are holding the orb and take psychic damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the psychic damage by 1d4.

An Arcane Focus takes a specific form and is bejeweled or carved to channel arcane magic. A Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard can use such an item as a Spellcasting Focus.

magic.name: Shavaran Chert Crystal
magic.desc:
An orb of shielding is made from crystal or stone aligned to one of the planes. While you are holding the orb and take force damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the force damage by 1d4.

An Arcane Focus takes a specific form and is bejeweled or carved to channel arcane magic. A Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard can use such an item as a Spellcasting Focus.

magic.name: Quori Celestine Orb
magic.desc:

An Arcane Focus takes a specific form and is bejeweled or carved to channel arcane magic. A Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard can use such an item as a Spellcasting Focus.

When you cast a spell that deals psychic damage, the spell gains a +1 bonus to one psychic damage roll of that spell.

Versatile. This weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property—the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack.

magic.desc:

magic.name: Summer Smoke Ring Festival Pipe
magic.desc:
An elegantly crafted pipe inlaid with silver accents and a pearl stem. The pipe is worth 1 gold piece and grants advantage on ability checks using it.

Pipes are made of clay or wood and used for inhaling the smoke of burning leaves of pipe-weed. A character that has proficiency with a pipe practises the art of smoking and likely has some skill at blowing smoke-rings. Smoking a pipe can aid you in efforts at introspection, and in friendly chatting with fellow practitioners of the art.

If you are proficient with pipes, you can spend one use of pipe-weed and at least one hour smoking your pipe to gain inspiration. You cannot use a pipe again in this way until you finish a long rest.

See the Tool Proficiencies entry for more information.

magic.name: Babble Pipes
magic.desc:
Made from pieces of several mismatched instruments, these panpipes have been tied together into a single, discordant whole.

Once a day, this instrument can be played as an Action, releasing a horrid symphony. Each creature in a 30 ft Emanation who can hear the music must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute.

A Frightened creature takes the Dash action and moves away from you by the safest route on each of its turns, unless there is nowhere to move. If the creature ends its turn in a space where it doesn't have line of sight to you, the creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends on that creature.

Tool (Musical Instrument). If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

magic.name: Boots of Soft Landing
magic.desc:
A pair of brown, fur-lined boots that have been finely crafted. The boots are quilted, and have ceramic soles that emit a colourful magical energy.

While wearing these boots, you always land on your feet and cannot be knocked Prone. Additionally, your fall speed is capped at 60 ft per round, and you take no damage from falling.

magic.name: Calling Quills
magic.desc:
These antique quills and writing pads were originally owned by siblings. When the family set up four different branches of their toy-making business across the continent, they developed the magical pads as an easy way to communicate orders and stock levels with one another.

When something is written on one of the four parchment pads, it is visible on all the other parchment pads. Messages are visible for 12 hours, at which point the pads magically absorb the ink.

magic.name: Gold Rings of Might
magic.desc:
These five ornate, golden rings once belonged to an evil monarch. Alone, each is simply an inert piece of dress jewellery. When they are brought together, they hum with dark and ominous energy.

The Gold Rings of Might have 5 charges, and regain 1 expended charge every day at dawn. If you expend the last charge, the item loses its enchantment and does not recharge. If a creature is wearing the Gold Rings of Might, they can innately cast the Shocking Grasp spell as a Magic action.

The wearer can expend 1 charge to cast Lightning Bolt (save DC 15) as a Magic action, without using the materials or a spell slot.

Alternatively, the wearer can expend 3 charges to cast Chain Lightning (save DC 15) as a Magic action, without using the materials or a spell slot.

magic.name: Goose Egg Healing Grenade
magic.desc:
Whether this smooth, pearlescent egg was truly laid by a mythical golden goose is the subject of much debate. What is known for sure, however, is that the egg has remarkable healing powers.

Once per day as an Action, this item can be thrown into an unoccupied space up to 40 ft away and release a wave of healing energy. Creatures within a 30 ft radius Sphere from the point the Goose Egg Healing Grenade lands regain 2d8 + 4 Hit Points, or 5d8 + 4 if they are within a 10 ft radius Sphere. The item's magic heals up to six creatures at a time, starting with the creatures with the lowest Hit Points.

This item's magic has no effect on undead creatures or constructs.

magic.name: Metronome Drum
magic.desc:
This neatly painted drum is attached to a leather shoulder harness, so it can be struck at waist height. Local folklore suggests that this instrument can have an almost hypnotic effect on those in earshot, but only if played at the correct tempo.

You can play this drum as an Action. Once a day, up to three Humanoids within a 30 ft Emanation of the drum beat must succeed on a DC 14 saving throw or have the Charmed condition and become Friendly towards you. The targets make their saving throws with advantage if you or your allies are fighting them. The Charmed condition ends after 1 hour or when you stop playing the drum. When the Charmed condition ends, the targets know they were Charmed by you.

Tool (Musical Instrument). If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

magic.name: Phial of Stoutmilk
magic.desc:
This thick glass bottle holds viscous, white, fizzing liquid. Tied around the bottle's neck is a worn tag that once listed the ingredients and stated dose.

For 1 hour after drinking this potion, when you take bludgeoning damage, reduce the total damage taken by 1d4. Your Strength and Constitution scores both increase by 2 until the potion's effects wear off.

magic.name: Swansong Staff
magic.desc:
This gnarled, oak staff ends in a crook reminiscent of a swan's neck. It is clearly ancient, and was only recently uncovered from deep within an elven ruin.

You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Once a day, if the wielder is reduced to 0 Hit Points, the Swansong Staff immediately animates (using the stats of an Animated Broom) to protect them. The weapon acts on the wielder's initiative. If the animated weapon is reduced to 0 Hit Points or if its wielder regains consciousness, it becomes inanimate once more.

Versatile. A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Mastery: Topple. If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

magic.name: Wand of Dancing
magic.desc:
Light glistens across this shiny, black wand; the ribbons that flow from its tip twinkle and sparkle in rhythmic patterns.

You can spin and twirl holding this wand to cast the Otto's Irresistible Dance spell (save DC 14). The wand can be used to cast the spell as many times as you like each day, however, once a creature fails its saving throw against the spell cast by this wand, the wand cannot be used to cast the spell again until dawn the next day.

magic.name: Animated Inks
magic.desc:
When you drink this potion, a type of creature you are thinking of appears as a tattoo on your skin. You choose the type of creature but its maximum Challenge Rating is determined by the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below.

You can take the Magic action to cause the tattoo to animate and move off your body, appearing in an unoccupied space of your choice within 60 feet. For the next 10 minutes, it uses the stat block of the chosen creature. During this time, the creature is Friendly to you and your allies. It understands your languages, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your Initiative count. If you issue no commands, the creature defends itself but takes no other action. At the end of the 10 minutes, or when the creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it returns to your body as a tattoo. Once you have used a Magic action to animate this tattoo, it can't be used again until 3 days pass.

If you end or lose Attunement to this magic item, the tattoo disappears and all other effects of this potion end.

RarityMaximum Challenge RatingUncommon1Rare3Very Rare7

magic.name: Bottle of Brew Tasting
magic.desc: This magic item is a glass bottle with a blank label on its front. When a potion or other liquid is poured into the bottle, the contents and effects of the liquid will appear, written in Common, on the label. This writing fades when the bottle is emptied of its contents.

magic.name: Bottomless Box of Treats
magic.desc:
This wondrous item has 5 charges. When you reach inside this box, you can expend a charge to pull out a treat. A Beast that eats the snack regains 3d4 + 3 Hit Points and removes one level of Exhaustion or ends one condition on it: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, or Paralyzed.

The box regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn.

magic.name: Coin of Easy Living
magic.desc: This Gold Piece appears mundane but, when flipped, always lands on the side you call while it is in the air. Additionally, you can summon it to your palm at will as a Bonus Action.

magic.name: Everfull Stein
magic.desc: This large ceramic stein is decorated with dwarven glyphs and topped with a brass lid that can be opened by thumb lever. While the lid is closed and the stein is empty, you can name a nonmagical ale, beer, or mead as a Bonus Action and the stein fills with that liquid.

magic.name: Last Rites Rum
magic.desc:
When you drink this potion, you take 2d4 Necrotic damage. For 1 hour, you have Resistance to Radiant damage, and whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Necrotic damage or its normal damage type.

This potion is thin and gray. It smells vaguely unpleasant but tastes like nothing at all.

magic.name: Loaded Dice
magic.desc:
This set of six-sided dice is indistinguishable from nonmagical dice. While attuned to the dice, you gain the following benefits.

Luck. The dice have 6 charges and regain 1d6 charges daily at dawn. When you fail a D20 Test, you can expend 1 charge to reroll the test if you don't have the Incapacitated condition. You must use the new roll.

Loaded. When you use this magic item to play a dice game, you have Advantage on ability checks made to determine the winner of the game.

magic.name: Medallion of Mettle
magic.desc: This ostentatious medallion draws the eye of even casual onlookers. Whenever you gain Temporary Hit Points, you gain an additional 1d6 Temporary Hit Points.

magic.name: Poundwise Porter
magic.desc:
For 1 minute after you drink this potion, you gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with your Unarmed Strikes.

This potion is thick and dark brown topped with a cream colored froth.

magic.name: Salamander Sauce
magic.desc:
When you drink this potion, you take 2d4 Fire damage. For 1 hour, you have Resistance to Cold damage and whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Fire damage or its normal damage type.

This potion is bright red and smells of hot peppers and spices. It is typically drizzled on food prior to eating but it is possible to consume it straight from the bottle.

magic.name: Bloodsbane
magic.desc:
This oil is deceptively clear and smells faintly like parchment, dried ink, and a touch of sulfur. To unlock the oil's power, an additional component must be mixed in (as shown in the Bloodsbane Effects table); this component may have already been added, or the oil's user can acquire an unmixed oil and add the component as part of a short or long rest. These components are difficult to sense once diluted in the oil, and identifying this oil may require a keen nose or additional research.

The oil can coat one slashing or piercing weapon or up to 5 pieces of slashing or piercing ammunition. Applying the oil in this way takes 1 minute, during which time a willing creature must offer one drop of their blood, mixing it into the oil to activate its magic.

A creature hit with a weapon or ammunition coated in this oil must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer an effect depending on the oil's special component added. In addition, if the creature fails the saving throw and the blood in the oil came from an illrigger, the creature has a seal placed on them by that illrigger. This seal doesn't count against the number of seals granted by the illrigger's Baleful Interdict feature.

magic.name: Adder Stone (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: These glassy stones are often found near the place where a marra was slain. Each Adder Stone is the size of a small fruit and has a natural hole in it. While you carry an Adder Stone, the first time you would gain the Paralyzed condition, the stone shatters and that condition is removed.

magic.name: Aether Blood
magic.desc:
The most extravagant rumors claim the creation of this glowing purple liquid requires the blood of a unicorn -- a creature generally regarded as mythical. Regardless of the truth, the potent magic in a vial of Aether Blood leads many spellcasters to carry it for use in dire circumstances.

Consuming this potion enhances your spellcasting prowess for 1 minute. While the effect lasts, add 1 to the saving throw DCs for the spells you cast. In addition, whenever your spell could be cast using a higher-level spell slot, increase the spell's effective level by 1.

Prolonged use of Aether Blood is grueling. You can consume it safely a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). Any further use results in painful addiction. While addicted, you have Disadvantage on Strength and Constitution ability checks and saving throws, and attack rolls against you have Advantage.

Consuming another vial of Aether Blood negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest, but you must also make a DC 10 Charisma save. On a failure, you become lethargic, and your Speed is reduced by 20 feet for 1 minute.

The addiction lasts until you receive a Greater Restoration spell, or until you have not consumed Aether Blood for 30 days.

magic.name: Amulet of Curse Suppression
magic.desc:
This glittering amulet of ivory and silver can be used to temporarily fend off the effects of curses. While attuned to the amulet, the effects of any curses on you are nullified, as though they had been removed by the Remove Curse spell.

However, this relief is only temporary. When the amulet is removed or you end your Attunement to it, any curses it was suppressing return with full force.

magic.name: Arc Rifle
magic.desc:
In the unforgiving lands of Etharis, having reliable and efficient weapons is as essential as carrying water and food.

In that regard, skilled inventors are highly sought, and among them gnomes are the most renowned. However, innovation can sometimes go too far, and the Arc Rifle is the perfect example of how.

This part-science, part-arcane contraption is a rifle-like weapon housing glass tubes of sparking electricity and powered by a small perpetual motion device. Invented by a team of famous gnome engineers, it literally shoots lightning, hitting the target faster than other missile weapons and reducing flesh to ashes in mere seconds. Due in part to this tremendous efficiency, this weapon was quickly declared illegal in most regions of Etharis. It is also believed to destroy the target's soul when it kills them.

The rifle has 4 charges. You can expend 1 charge as a Magic action to launch a torrent of lightning in a 60-foot long, 5-foot-wide Line. Each creature in the Line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 Lightning damage, or half as much on a successful save.

Regaining Charges. The rifle regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll

1d20. On a 1, the rifle becomes a useless hunk of metal and glass.

magic.name: Arcane Oil (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This substance is created by distilling the jelly that encases the brain of a xakalonus. You can take a Bonus Action to coat one weapon or up to 20 pieces of ammunition. If the coated objects are not magical, for the next minute, your attacks with the coated weapon or ammunition gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls. If the coated objects are magical, they instead gain the ability to ignore the hraptnon's Immunity to magical weapons.

magic.name: Banshee Box
magic.desc:
This ivory music box is inlaid with silver decorations depicting tiny scenes of gruesome violence. If a creature holds the box for at least one minute, they can use a Magic action to mentally command the box to make a sound or phrase of their choosing, lasting up to one minute. Once the lid is open, that sound or phrase continues to play on a loop until the box is closed. If the person who created the repeating sound travels more than 300 feet away from the box, the lid closes and the music box ceases to play.

The box can create any soundscape, like haunting piano music, the sounds of a lively party, a spoken phrase, or a continuous series of screams. When the Magic action is used to create the sounds, the user can also choose whether the sound is audible in an Emanation with a 5-foot radius, a 30-foot radius, or a 120-foot radius.

magic.name: Blessed Reliquary
magic.desc:
This small wooden or ivory box holds a piece of a saint. While it is on your person, you gain the following benefits:

You have Advantage on saving throws caused by Undead creatures. You can use each of your Channel Divinity class features one additional time. When you use Turn Undead, you may choose for the targets to have Disadvantage on their saving throws. This can be used once. You regain its use after a Long Rest.

magic.name: Bliss
magic.desc:
The magical drug comes in the form of a small, round pellet of white powder. If ingested by a Humanoid, that creature is filled with feelings of calm and happiness.

Upon ingestion, you have the following effects for 1d4 hours:

- You have Immunity to the Frightened condition.
- You gain 3d10 Temporary Hit Points.
- Your Speed is reduced by 15 feet.
- You have Disadvantage on D20 Tests.
- If you cause another creature to make a saving throw, it has Advantage on that save.
- After the effects wear off, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, or you gain 1 Exhaustion level.

magic.name: Blood Capsule
magic.desc:
This cylindrical flask is etched with arcane runes.

Humanoid blood stored in the blood capsule remains fresh for up to one year. The flask stores enough blood to sustain a vampire for one day.

magic.name: Cap of Bravery (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: Woven from the remains of an old snarite, this cap provides the wearer with a sense of magical peace and calm that emanates from them. While wearing this cap, you radiate an aura in a 30-foot Emanation. You and allies in this aura have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end effects that include the Frightened condition

magic.name: Cloak of the Listener (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This is a cloak made of ears that were once part of a swarm of ears. It pulses gently and oozes yellow fluid from its many holes. While wearing this cloak, you can take an action to create one of two effects:

Ooze. You tug the cloak to create a puddle of waxy goo that covers the ground in a 10-foot square centered on a point within 30 feet of you. A creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or have the Grappled condition (escape DC 15). This wax remains for 1 minute. Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Hide. You completely conceal your head with the cloak. You have the Blinded condition, you have Blindsight with a range of 120 feet, and you can hear all speech within 120 feet regardless of obstructions. These effects last for 1 minute. Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Cloak of the Mausgeist (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This fine garment is made of mausgeist fur with a silk lining. While wearing it, you gain the following benefits:

Heightened Senses. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

Magic Protection. You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Charm. You can take an action to cast the Charm Person spell (save DC 13). Once used, this property of the cloak can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Cloak of the Stygian Bat (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This cloak is made from stygian bat hides and bristles with coarse black hair. While wearing the cloak, you have Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

In addition, you can take an action to gain a Fly Speed of 30 feet for one minute. While this effect is active, you also have blindsight with a range of 120 feet, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws while in the air. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Cloak of Therianthropy (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This spotted grey cloak is made of styrkvisnar hide. While wearing it, you have Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks.

Additionally, you can take an action to transform into a wolf, eagle, or seal for up to 1 hour. The transformation otherwise functions as the Polymorph spell, but you can take a Bonus Action to revert to your normal form. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Coat of Lies (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This coat is made from the tongues of a harvester of lies' victims. While you wear it, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class and you have Advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks.

The cloak has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. You can use a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge while wearing the cloak to enhance the next spell you cast before the start of your next turn, allowing that spell to be cast without any Verbal or Somatic components.

magic.name: Coin of War and Fear
magic.desc:
This dark metal coin is a token of heretical dogma that claims Empyreus and Beleth are one and the same. One side bears the Empyreus's icon, while the other shows Beleth's leering face.

While holding this coin, you can take an action to flip it. Roll a d6. The icon of Empyreus shows on an even number, granting you the Boon of Empyreus. On an odd number, Beleth shows and confers the Boon of Beleth.

Boon of Empyreus. For one minute, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class, and you add 1d4 to the first attack roll you make each of your turns. If you would receive this boon again before the next dawn, you instead take 3d6 Radiant damage and the boon is not applied.

Boon of Beleth. For one minute, an aura radiates from you in a 10-foot radius. When an enemy ends its turn in the area, it must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. While the aura lasts, you deal an extra 1d6 Psychic damage whenever you hit a Frightened creature with a weapon attack. If you would receive this boon again before the next dawn, you instead take 3d6 Necrotic damage and the boon is not applied.

magic.name: Collar of the Undead
magic.desc:
Some people have no qualms about exploiting any opportunity for profit, including the sorrow caused by the loss of a loved one. Such people would appreciate the Collar of the Undead, whether as con artists looking for bereaved individuals to fleece, or as dark sorcerers in need of souls.

As an action, you can place this collar around the neck of a Humanoid creature of Large size or smaller that has died within the last 10 days. The creature returns to life with 1 Hit Point. The creature uses its normal game statistics, except that its creature type becomes Undead and it doesn't need to eat, sleep, or breathe. If its Hit Points are reduced to 0, the creature is utterly destroyed, turning into dust.

Each dawn, the creature's Hit Point Maximum decreases by 1d4 as its soul slowly slips away. When the creature's Hit Point Maximum reaches 0, or its Hit Points are reduced to 0, it falls apart into a heap of dust and is destroyed.

On each of your turns, you can take a Bonus Action to mentally command the creature if it is within 60 feet of you, and it follows your orders to the best of your ability. If you issue no commands, the creature takes the Dodge action and moves only to avoid harm. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

If the collar is removed, the creature is immediately reduced to 0 Hit Points.

magic.name: Crimson Mist
magic.desc:
This tiny bottle contains a cocktail of pheromones from creatures of prey. As an action, you spray the pheromones on one target within 5 feet, and its effect lasts for 1 minute.

Beasts or other creatures that must attack the nearest creature will target the affected individual instead, as long as that individual is within 60 feet of the attacker.

magic.name: Dreams Leaves
magic.desc:
Made from a mysterious, magically grown plant, this popular new drug induces vivid hallucinations in which the user's dreams appear to be fulfilled. Some users even see visions of branching possibilities that their life could take.

Upon consuming Dreams Leaves, you can choose to fall into a blissful, trance-like state for 1 hour, during which time you have the Unconscious condition. Taking damage ends the trance early.

If you remain in the trance for the full hour, you awaken with a faint insight into your future. Once before you finish your next Long Rest, you can take a Reaction to reroll a D20 Test and use the new result.

Using this Reaction creates an addiction to Dreams Leaves. While addicted, you have Disadvantage on saving throws. Consuming another dose of Dreams Leaves negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest.

The addiction lasts until you receive a Greater Restoration spell, or until you have not consumed Dreams Leaves for 30 days.

magic.name: Elixir of Elemental Spittle (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This foul-smelling liquid is made from the saliva of an elemental troll. For one minute after consuming the potion, you can take a Bonus Action to spit energy at a creature within 5 feet of you. The target must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 damage of a type corresponding to the troll whose spittle was used to craft the potion. No damage is inflicted on a successful save.

If the target rolls a natural 20 on its saving throw, the potion explodes inside you. You take 6d6 damage of the type listed for it, and the potion's duration ends immediately.

magic.name: Enchanted Feather (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This magical feather can sometimes be found growing from a rabenhex. While holding the feather, you can take an action to cast Remove Curse. Afterward, the feather becomes nonmagical.

magic.name: Faerie Crown
magic.desc:
This crown is woven of aromatic flowers. When you first don the crown after attuning to it, 1d6 + 3 butterflies begin fluttering around it.

When you are hit by a melee attack, you can take a Reaction to release one of the butterflies. The attack misses you and destroys the butterfly instead.

Once all butterflies are destroyed, the crown withers and crumbles to dust.

magic.name: Fin Symbiote
magic.desc:
This tendril of flesh, harvested from an Aberration, melds with the body of its host. If you are a Humanoid, you can attune to this item by stitching it into your skin during the Attunement process. At the end of this time, the fin burrows into your body and bonds with your muscular system. Non-Humanoids cannot attune to the Fin Symbiote.

While attuned to the symbiote, you gain the following benefits:

Symbiotic Health. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws.

Immovable. When you would be moved against your will, you can take a Reaction to subtract 10 feet from that movement.

Aberrant Power. If you have achieved at least Stage 1 of the Aberrant Horror Transformation, add +2 to the DC of save DCs for your Aberrant Horror Boons.

Symbiote Link. You cannot voluntarily end your Attunement to this magic item. If it is physically removed from your body, it regrows in 1d4 hours unless you receive a Remove Curse spell before it grows back (which also ends your Attunement).

magic.name: Flammable Tincture (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This swirling mixture of red and white liquid is formed from the remains of a coldfire ooze. As an action, the vial of Flammable Tincture can be hurled up to 30 feet at a target, which must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or be covered with the liquid. For 1 minute, the creature loses its Immunity or Resistance to Fire damage and has Vulnerability to Fire damage instead.

magic.name: Full Moon Extract
magic.desc:
This potent powder is supposedly created by grinding up the dried organs of a werewolf. Despite the risks associated with its use, it is a favored drug of many wrestlers, boxers, and soldiers because of the raw strength it provides.

Consuming this potion enhances your physical prowess for 1 hour. While the effect lasts, your Strength score becomes 19 (unless it was already 19 or higher), and you have Advantage on Strength ability checks and saving throws.

Prolonged use of Full Moon Extract is risky. You can consume it safely a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). Any further use results in painful addiction. While addicted, you have Disadvantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws, and attack rolls against you have Advantage.

Consuming another dose of Full Moon Extract negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest, but you must also make a DC 10 Charisma save. On a failure, you become overcome by violent urges for 1 minute. During that time, you cannot take Bonus Actions or Reactions. At the start of each of your turns, you regard the creature nearest to you that you can see or hear as your enemy. During that turn, you must move as close to the creature as possible and take the Attack action, targeting the creature. If your movement doesn't bring you within reach, you must use your Dash action to continue moving toward it.

The addiction lasts until you receive a Greater Restoration spell, or until you have not consumed Full Moon Ex

magic.name: Funeral Mask
magic.desc:
This delicate mask is made of thinly beaten copper that molds to the skin when worn. While wearing this mask, you can use an action to alter your appearance, including your height, weight, facial features, the sound of your voice, hair length, coloration, and distinguishing characteristics for 8 hours. You can make yourself appear as a member of another species, though none of your statistics change. You also can't appear as a creature of a different size, and your basic shape stays the same; if you're bipedal, you can't use this item to become quadrupedal, for instance.

Creatures within 5 feet of you can use an action to make a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check to discern your true appearance.

If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Lich Transformation, you also gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class while your appearance is disguised by the mask.

Once you use the mask, you cannot do so again until the following dawn.

magic.name: Gold Boar Ring (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: The ring, made from the bristles of the gold mane boar, sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. This light shines even in areas where magic does not function, or where magical light would normally be suppressed.

magic.name: Grenade of Remorse (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This substance, harvested from the tears of a remorseful storm, proves toxic to creatures of unnatural origins. You can take an action to hurl the grenade at a point up to 30 feet away. When it lands, the grenade explodes in a 20-foot-radius Sphere. Each Aberration, Fiend, and Undead creature within the area makes a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 8d6 Psychic damage on a failed save or half that much on a successful one.

magic.name: Gristaline (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This gruesome mixture is made from ground mouruge bones, along with rotten meat and mud. When consumed, your Strength score becomes 19 for 1 hour (unless it is already 19 or higher). You also have Disadvantage on Intelligence ability checks and saving throws for the duration.

magic.name: Heaven's Herald
magic.desc:
This golden trumpet is never dulled by rust or dirt. As an action, you can blow the trumpet to create a rousing battle call that can be heard up to 600 feet away.

When you use the trumpet, choose up to 12 willing creatures within 600 feet to become emboldened. An emboldened creature has Immunity to the Frightened condition and Advantage on Wisdom saving throws. In addition, its Hit Point maximum increases by 2d10 and it regains the same number of Hit Points. These benefits last for 8 hours.

If you are a Fiend or Undead creature, you take 8d6 Radiant damage when you blow the trumpet.

Once you use Heaven's Herald, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Hogs' Wash (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This foul-tasting tea is brewed from the powdered tusks of doom boars. When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of a Remove Curse spell.

Hogs' Wash can also be used as a component in removing a Shadowsteel curse (see "Shadowsteel Curses").

magic.name: Humble Frock
magic.desc:
While wearing this frock and not wearing any armor, Opportunity Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage.

If you have reached at least Stage 2 of the Seraph Transformation, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid revealing your true nature.

magic.name: Hunter's Zeal
magic.desc: This glowing green liquid sends a creature's immune system into a hyperactive state. When you drink this potion, you have Immunity to Poison damage and to the Poisoned condition for 1 hour. While the effect lasts, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid becoming cursed. When the potion's effect ends, you gain 1 level of Exhaustion.

magic.name: Inquisitor's Draught
magic.desc: Designed to aid in the capture and interrogation of mages, this silver syrup is also an effective method of freeing oneself from a cursed item. After drinking this potion, you are incapable of attuning to magic items for 1 hour. During this duration, you can take an action to sever all your Attunements to magic items (even cursed items). At the end of this duration, if you are attuned to any magic items, you die.

magic.name: Iron Fangs
magic.desc: These iron tooth caps are inscribed with magical runes. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with your Bite attacks, and your Bite attacks deal your choice of either force or Piercing damage.

magic.name: Knifewing Cape (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This cloak is made from the skin of twenty knifewings. While wearing it, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. If you fall, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling.

magic.name: Lindwyrm Venom (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This terrible venom is extracted and distilled from the deadly lindwyrm. It can be delivered via ingestion or a wound. A creature exposed to the venom must succeed on a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or take 8d8 Poison damage and have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. While Poisoned, the creature has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity skill checks and saving throws.

magic.name: Lycanthropy Antidote (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: Made with fzeg blood, this silvery potion is dotted with swirling flecks of red. Drinking this liquid removes the curse of lycanthropy.

magic.name: Magebane Bomb (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This bubbling liquid is distilled from the remains of a magebane ooze. You can throw the container at an enemy's weapon or armor, or at a spellcaster.

Make a ranged weapon attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 Acid damage. If the weapon was targeted, that weapon takes a -1 penalty to attacks and damage as well. If armor was targeted, that armor takes a -1 penalty to the Armor Class. Both effects end after the wielder or wearer completes a Long Rest.

A spellcaster hit with a Magebane Bomb has a -1 penalty to hit with spell attacks, and the DCs of saving throws against spells they cast decrease by 1 for 1 minute.

magic.name: Magical Prosthetics
magic.desc:
The brutal warfare and vicious monsters prevalent across Etharis leave many with Grievous Wounds, including missing limbs and other potentially debilitating injuries. The engineers and crafters of the world have made great strides in helping those people deal with those injuries through Prosthetics, which are covered in Chapter 5 of the Grim Hollow Player's Guide.

Magical versions of Prosthetics can be crafted with properties that mimic existing Wondrous Items or Rings. Typically, these Prosthetics replicate the body part that would wear that item. For example, a Magical Prosthetic leg could replicate the effect of Boots of Elvenkind, while a Magical Prosthetic hand might act as a Ring of Protection.

A Magical Prosthetic has the same rarity as the magic item it mimics. It counts as "wearing" an item of that kind, so if you have a Magical Prosthetic leg that mimics Boots of Elvenkind, you can't wear another pair of magic boots.

magic.name: Mortal Coil
magic.desc:
This ring is composed of hundreds of rose gold wires woven to coil around the finger. It allows its wearer's spirit to resist the pull of the afterlife.

If you die while wearing this ring, your soul enters the ring and your body remains alive and Stable at 0 Hit Points. When you regain Hit Points, your soul reenters your body and the ring turns into a useless lump of lead.

magic.name: Muscle Graft (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
Created through a gruesome process requiring the muscle tissue of a bugbear vampire, this graft melds to the flesh of a living creature who attunes to it. Your Strength increases by 2, to a maximum of 30. When you become attuned, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or your Constitution decreases by 2, to a minimum of 1.

Curse. This graft is cursed. Attuning to it curses you for 1 year or until you are targeted by Remove Curse or a similar spell. Removing the graft fails to end the curse on you, and you cannot end the Attunement while the curse lasts. You develop a deep desire for rare meat and raw blood. At the end of each week, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or become a Vampire Spawn with no progenitor.

magic.name: Net of Maiden's Hair (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: Sewn from the plant creature known as maiden's hair, this sweet-smelling piece of headgear bestows lingering magical properties. While wearing the net on your head, you have Advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks. Additionally, you can take a Bonus Action to make an ability check to end the Grappled condition, and you have Advantage on ability checks to end the Grappled condition.

magic.name: Nightmare Staff (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This twisted staff is created from the remains of a marra. It has 3 charges and regains its expended charges daily at dusk.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you damages you while you hold this staff, you can take a Reaction to expend 1 of the staff's charges to force the creature to make a DC 13 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, the creature sees a phantasm that causes it to have the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. If the creature is already Frightened, it also takes 2d6 Psychic damage.

Versatile. A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Mastery: Topple. If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

magic.name: Pharazorthok Sprout
magic.desc:
This hand-sized fleshy sapling has writhing tentacles for branches and bulbous yellow eyes studding its trunk. You can take an action to plant it in the ground in your space, at which point it begins whispering telepathically to you. While the sprout is planted and within 30 feet of you, you have truesight with a range of 30 feet.

Anyone in the sprout's space can take an action to uproot it. If left in the ground for 1 minute, the sprout experiences a growth surge, uproots itself, and becomes a Roper that is Hostile to you and your allies.

magic.name: Potion of Glacial Resistance (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This brew is made from the ground horns of keppmirs. When consumed, this potion allows you to breathe underwater for 1 hour, during which time you have Resistance to Cold damage. It tastes salty and gives off a slight warmth.

magic.name: Potion of Harm (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This concoction is the result of a failed attempt to make a Potion of Heal. It is indistinguishable from that potion without using divination magic of level 3 or higher.

When you imbibe this potion, roll 1d4. That becomes your new Hit Point total. If the Potion of Harm is given to a creature with 0 Hit Points, they instantly suffer a Death Saving Throw failure and begin dying if they are Stable.

magic.name: Potion of Heal (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This ebon liquid is made from the remains of a downcast vampire. When you imbibe this potion, you regain all your Hit Points.

magic.name: Potion of Life Sharing (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This shimmering liquid changes colors constantly within its vial. Made from the acid glands of the dreaded wolfentroika, this potion allows you to share your life force with others. After drinking this potion, you can take a Bonus Action to choose a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see or hear. That creature regains 4d6 Hit Points, and you take an equal amount of Necrotic damage, which can't be reduced or prevented in any way. The effect ends after 1 minute, at which point you gain 1 level of Exhaustion.

magic.name: Potion of Relentlessness (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This viscous potion is made from quoxxarie blood. After drinking this potion, when you are reduced to 0 Hit Points you can expend a Hit Point Dice (no action required) and set your Hit Points to 1. This effect lasts for 1 minute, at the end of which you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of Exhaustion for each Hit Die spent during the potion's duration.

magic.name: Profane Charm
magic.desc: This charm is a charred feather harvested from a fallen angel, wrapped in silver wire. While you wear this charm, your creature type appears to be Humanoid for the purpose of Detect Evil and Good and similar effects.

magic.name: Queen's Token
magic.desc:
This humble acorn is one of the mightiest gifts a Faerie queen can bestow upon her subjects. While holding the acorn, you can cast the Wish spell. After using the acorn in this way, it immediately teleports back to the queen who bestowed it.

If the Wish spell is used in a way that the queen would perceive as a threat to herself or her realm, the spell does not work. Instead, the creature who made the wish immediately transforms into an oak tree. Only a Wish spell cast with the Queen's Token can return a creature transformed in this way to its original state.

magic.name: Ready Gunk (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This sticky paste is fashioned from the powdered bone armor of a bone trader. After you treat a weapon, Shield, or other item that can be wielded in one or two hands with the paste, you can take a Bonus Action to summon and equip it, as long as the item is within 30 feet of you. After using this effect three times, it loses its potency.

magic.name: Resuscitation Bomb (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This foul-smelling concoction is made from the remains of stinking sludge. As an action, you can throw the vial up to 10 feet, where it breaks and releases a noxious vapor that fills a 30-foot-radius Sphere. Each creature in the area with the Incapacitated, Stunned, or Unconscious condition ends those conditions. Each dying creature in the area has Advantage on its next Death Saving Throw. Each creature that was not dying and did not have any of those conditions must instead succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

magic.name: Ring of Hidden Desire
magic.desc: This rose gold band is set with an obsidian stone carved in the shape of a heart. While wearing this ring, you can use a Magic action to attempt to learn a creature's darkest desire. Select a creature that you can see. That creature must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you immediately learn the target's greatest desire. On a successful save, you do not learn anything, and the creature is immune to the effects of the ring. If the creature you choose has an Intelligence of 3 or lower, the creature is unaffected. The ring's power can be used once and recharges at midnight.

magic.name: Ring of Nightmares (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This ring's crafting requires powdered brain from a restless lumberer. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can take a Bonus Action to expend 1 charge to change the damage type of the next spell you cast before the end of your turn to Psychic damage.

In addition, while attuned to the ring, you're Immune to spells or magical abilities that interfere with your sleep or cause nightmares while you sleep.

magic.name: Ring of Radiation
magic.desc: This ring is made of braided copper wire. While wearing this ring, your elemental energies are supercharged, allowing them to radiate from your body. When you cast a spell or use an ability that does Cold, Fire, or Lightning damage, the range of the spell or ability is doubled.

magic.name: Ring of Veracity
magic.desc:
This golden band is stamped with images of smiling humanoid faces. While attuned to this ring, the wearer has Advantage on Search actions to make a Wisdom (Insight) check.

Additionally, you can take a Magic action to cast Zone of Truth (save DC 15) with the ring. The ring can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Rod of Ruin
magic.desc:
This rod is formed of stacked crystal spheres filled with smoke. The rod has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dusk.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you damages you while you are holding this rod, you can take a Reaction to expend 1 charge to force the creature to make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature gains 1 level of Exhaustion. If you have the Lich Transformation, the creature has Disadvantage on its saving throw, and you gain 2d10 Temporary Hit Points when a creature fails the save.

magic.name: Rod of the Pack Master
magic.desc:
This rod appears to be a piece of driftwood carved with images of wolves and bears. While holding the rod, you can take a Magic action to cast Polymorph on any number of willing Humanoids you can see within 30 feet of you. The only forms you can choose for each target are Black Bear and Wolf, and the targets retain their Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. The effect lasts for 24 hours and requires no Concentration. You can take a Magic action to end the effect early for any number of targets.

Once you use the rod to cast Polymorph, it can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Lycanthrope Transformation, you can hold this rod in your teeth and use it while in hybrid or kindred form.

magic.name: Sangromancer's Vial
magic.desc:
This vial of red glass and gold filigree is useful to practitioners of blood magic. As part of the Attunement process, you fill the vial with your own blood. Choose up to 10 of your Hit Point Dice and roll them, reducing your Hit Point maximum by an amount equal to the result. This creates a pool of Hit Dice that you can expend in place of your own when you cast a Sangromancy spell.

Each time you finish a Long Rest, the pool is replenished, restoring a number of Hit Dice equal to half the number you rolled during Attunement.

If you end your Attunement to the vial, your Hit Point maximum returns to normal after you finish a Long Rest.

magic.name: Sizzling Serum (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: Created from the ichor in a potbelly's stomach-pot, this volatile concoction is effective at damaging inorganic substances. As a Magic action, you can hurl the serum at a Construct or an object that you can see within 30 feet of you. The target makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 10d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

magic.name: Soulbond Stone
magic.desc:
This smooth and weighty stone has a dusk-colored gem embedded in its center. When pressed to the chest of a creature who has been dead for less than one minute, the stone captures a fragment of the dead creature's soul for later use.

The Soulbond Stone has 3 charges. While holding the stone, you can expend 1 charge to cast Speak With Dead with the stone, as if the trapped soul's corpse was the target of the spell. When the last charge is expended, the stone shatters and the soul fragment returns to its rightful place.

magic.name: Staff of Briars (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
This wooden staff is made from the harvested claws of a braerog. It has 10 charges. While holding the staff, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge and cause thorn-covered rose vines to sprout up, covering a 20-foot square centered on a point within 5 feet of you. This area becomes Difficult Terrain.

Once created, the briars are non-magical. They grow (or wither) as appropriate for the environment, just as a normal plant would.

The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff turns into rose petals and is lost forever.

Versatile. A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Mastery: Topple. If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

magic.name: Staff of the Sorcerer King
magic.desc:
This ebony staff bears a bronze spear tip and additional blades carved to depict a winged scarab. The staff can be wielded as a magic spear that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. You are considered proficient with this weapon while you are attuned to it, even if you aren't proficient with spears. While holding the staff, you gain these benefits:

Spell Power. You gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls.

Cull Subjects. Humanoids have a -2 penalty to saving throws against your spells.

Spell Shield. You have Advantage on saving throws against spells that target only you.

Cursed. This staff is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with Remove Curse or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the staff, keeping it within reach at all times. In addition, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls made with weapons other than this one.

While cursed, you must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw each day at midnight. On a failed save, your Hit Point maximum is reduced by 10 unless you are Undead. Your Hit Point maximum can only be restored by a Wish spell. If your Hit Point maximum is reduced to 0 while cursed, you die and immediately rise as a Wight.

magic.name: Stalk Symbiote
magic.desc:
This ocular organ, harvested from a living Aberration, melds with the skull of its host. If you are a Humanoid, you can attune to this item by stitching it into your scalp during the Attunement process. At the end of this time, the stalk burrows into your skull and bonds with your brain. Non-Humanoids cannot attune to the Stalk Symbiote.

While attuned to this item, you gain the following benefits:

Symbiotic Senses. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks, and you do not have Disadvantage on Initiative rolls when surprised.

Aberrant Power. If you have achieved at least Stage 1 of the Aberrant Horror Transformation, you have blindsight with a range of 10 feet.

Symbiote Link. You cannot voluntarily end your Attunement to the Stalk Symbiote. If it is physically removed from your body, it regrows in 1d4 hours unless you receive a Remove Curse spell before it grows back (which also ends your Attunement).

magic.name: Star Metal Ring (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This heavy steel ring is set with a chunk of shimmering star metal. While wearing this ring, your appendages are crusted with iridescent star metal. Your Unarmed Strikes are considered magical and deal Force damage.

magic.name: Straitjacket
magic.desc:
This stained grey jacket has long arms reaching the floor and contains dozens of restraining straps. This magical jacket takes 10 minutes to don or doff. While wearing this item and not wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you add your Intelligence modifier to your Armor Class. Also, you can cast spells without using Somatic or Material components that don't have a GP value listed. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes.

If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Aberrant Horror Transformation, you may roll twice whenever rolling on the Unstable Form table and choose either result.

magic.name: Suit of the Lamb (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc: This suit of comfortable woolen clothes, made from the wool of the rare and dangerous poffer, includes a shirt, trousers or a kilt, and thick socks. While wearing the suit, you have Resistance to Lightning damage, and you don't suffer effects from extreme cold weather.

magic.name: Sun Shades
magic.desc: These black leather goggles are set with cloudy glass that completely obscures the eyes of the wearer. You can take an action to don or doff these goggles. While wearing these goggles, you ignore your Sunlight Sensitivity, as well as any other ill effects you would suffer due to exposure to sunlight. The goggles also block your Darkvision, preventing you from seeing in the dark.

magic.name: Talisman of Tormach (GH:CG'24)
magic.desc:
The dreadful talisman is crafted from the skull at the center of a gore elemental. When you kill a creature with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike while you wear the talisman, you gain 10 Temporary Hit Points for 1 minute.

While you have any of these Temporary Hit Points, your melee weapon attacks and Unarmed Strikes deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage on a hit.

magic.name: Thought Talker Orbs
magic.desc:
This magical spying device, designed by gnome engineers on behalf of the Ebon Syndicate, is composed of two crystal orbs. The Emitter Orb is marble-sized, making it easy to slip into your target's purse or pocket. The Receiver Orb is fist-sized.

You can take a Magic action and touch the two orbs together to activate them for 7 days. Once activated, the Emitter Orb begins capturing thoughts within a 5-foot Sphere centered on it. A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, that creature is immune to the effect for 24 hours. On a failed save, the holder of the Received Orb becomes immediately aware of that creature's surface thoughts for 1 minute, even if it leaves the area.

magic.name: Thricecall Mirror
magic.desc:
This ornate hand mirror, made of carved iron and adorned with images of grasping hands, can be used to contact other planes. As a Magic action, you can speak the true name of an extraplanar being, such as a Fey, Fiend, or Celestial, into the mirror three times. This summons the named creature in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the mirror.

A creature summoned this way retains its free will, and there is no guarantee it views you as an ally. It cannot leave this plane for 1 minute, after which time it automatically returns to its home plane unless it has the means to travel between planes on its own, in which case it can choose to stay.

magic.name: Toadstool Toddy
magic.desc: This carbonated liquid, a potent distillation of faerie magic, is bright fuchsia and tastes of autumn rain. A Humanoid who drinks a Toadstool Toddy has Immunity to Fire and Cold damage for 1 hour.

magic.name: Vilesmog Bomb
magic.desc: This smoky concoction is a favorite of poisoners and assassins. You can use a Magic action to throw this vial up to 30 feet away from you, at which point it breaks and releases a dark vapor that fills a 15-foot-radius Sphere centered on it for 2 rounds. A creature that enters the area or starts its turn there loses any Resistance or Immunity to Poison damage and has Vulnerability to Poison damage. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

magic.name: Wand of the Poltergeist
magic.desc:
This wand is a swirl of dark and white wood, topped with a carved screaming skull. The wand has 7 charges.

With the wand in hand, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: Animate Objects (4 charges), Major Image (3 charges), or Shatter (2 charges).

Regaining Charges. The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll a d20. On a 20, the wand explodes into splinters and is destroyed.

magic.name: Wraps of Aphaeleon
magic.desc: Aphaeleon is the Arch Seraph of temperance and spiritual balance, a patron to many monks. While wearing these simple cloth fist wraps endowed with his blessing, you can spend 3 Focus Points on your turn to end the Incapacitated, Paralyzed, or Stunned condition on yourself (no action required).

magic.name: Adder Stone (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc: These glassy stones are often found near the place where a Marra was slain. Each Adder Stone is the size of a small fruit and has a natural hole in it. While you carry an Adder Stone, the first time you would gain the Paralyzed condition, the stone shatters and that condition is removed.

magic.name: Arcane Oil (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc: This substance is created by distilling the jelly that encases the brain of a Xakalonus. You can take a Bonus Action to coat one weapon or up to 20 pieces of ammunition. If the coated objects are not magical, for the next minute, your attacks with the coated weapon or ammunition gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls. If the coated objects are magical, they instead gain the ability to ignore the Hraptnon's Immunity to magical weapons.

magic.name: Bat Wings of Flying
magic.desc:
This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.

Someone who has proficiency in Leatherworker's Tools can make this cloak in 5 days, using reagents worth 500 GP. Somebody must cast Fly on the cloak on three out of the five days of its making. These wings give you a Fly Speed of only 40 feet, but they can be used once every 1d8 hours.

magic.name: Blight Effigy
magic.desc:
This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.

Someone who has proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies, Arcana, Nature, or Medicine can remove the heart of a Blightwalker. Treated with reagents worth 100 GP, wrapped in an iron chain, and dried in the sun for 3 days, the heart can become a magic item called a Blight Effigy. Creating this Blight Effigy using this process requires a successful DC 13 Intelligence or Wisdom check with the proficiency used. Someone holding the heart can use an action to squeeze it, casting Blight as a 4th-level spell with a saving throw DC of 15. Once the heart casts the spell, it and the chain binding it crumble to dust.

magic.name: Blightscale Dragon Scale Mail
magic.desc:
This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.

Someone who has proficiency with Smith's Tools or Leatherworker's Tools can fashion the scales of an Adult or Ancient Blightscale Dragon into Dragon Scale Mail. Doing so takes 10 days and other materials worth 5,000 GP. The armor offers no protection against Frightful Presence but grants Resistance to Necrotic damage and Poison damage

While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class, you have Advantage on saving throws against the breath weapons of Dragons, and you have Resistance to {{getFullImmRes item.resist}} damage.

Additionally, you can focus your senses as a Magic action to discern the distance and direction to the closest {{item.detail1}} dragon within 30 miles of yourself. This action can't be used again until the next dawn.

The wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

magic.name: Bloodbonded Blood
magic.desc:
This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.

One vial of this blood can be harvested from a single Bloodbonded with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check. Drinking it within one day causes the user to be under the effect of a Bless spell. When the spell ends, the user gains 1 Exhaustion level.

magic.name: Cadeer Wand
magic.desc:
This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.

A Cadeer Antler can be fashioned into a Wand suitable as a Spellcasting Focus for arcane spellcasters and druids. If made into a magic item, this Wand has 1 extra charge per day. Also, once per day and at the cost of 1 charge thereafter, a magic Wand of Cadeer horn grants the wielder a d4 that can be rolled when the wielder makes a spellcasting ability check to see if Dispel Magic or Counterspell works. The wielder adds the number rolled on the d4 to the spellcasting ability check, or the counterspelled creature subtracts the d4 from its saving throw.

A Druidic Focus takes a specific form and is carved, tied with ribbon, or painted to channel primal magic. A Druid or Ranger can use such an object as a Spellcasting Focus.

magic.name: Cap of Bravery (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc: Woven from the remains of an Old Snarite, this cap provides the wearer with a sense of magical peace and calm that emanates from them. While wearing this cap, you radiate an aura in a 30-foot Emanation. You and allies in this aura have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end effects that include the Frightened condition.

magic.name: Cloak of the Listener (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc:
This is a cloak made of ears that were once part of a Swarm of Ears. It pulses gently and oozes yellow fluid from its many holes. While wearing this cloak, you can take a Magic action to create one of two effects:

Ooze. You tug the cloak to create a puddle of waxy goo that covers the ground in a 10-foot square centered on a point within 30 feet of you. A creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or have the Grappled condition (escape DC 15). This wax remains for 1 minute.

Hide. You completely conceal your head with the cloak. You have the Blinded condition, you have Blindsight with a range of 120 feet, and you can hear all speech within 120 feet regardless of obstructions. These effects last for 1 minute.

Once each effect is used, that effect can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Cloak of the Mausgeist (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc:
This fine garment is made of Mausgeist fur with a silk lining. While wearing it, you gain the following benefits:

Heightened Senses. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

Magic Protection. You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Charm. You can take a Magic action to cast the Charm Person spell (save DC 13). Once used, this property of the cloak can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Cloak of the Stygian Bat (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc:
This cloak is made from Stygian Bat hides and bristles with coarse black hair, While wearing the cloak, you have Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

In addition, you can take a Magic action to gain a Fly Speed of 30 feet for one minute. While this effect is active, you also have Blindsight with a range of 120 feet, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws while in the air. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Cloak of Therianthropy (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc:
This spotted grey cloak is made of Styrkvisnar hide. While wearing it, you have Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks.

Additionally, you can take a Magic action to transform into a wolf, eagle, or seal for up to 1 hour. The transformation otherwise functions as the Polymorph spell, but you can take a Bonus Action to revert to your normal form. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

magic.name: Coat of Lies (GH:MG'24)
magic.desc:
This coat is made from the tongues of a harvester of lies' victims. While you wear it, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class and you have Advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks.

The coat has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. You can use a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge while wearing the coat to enhance the next spell you cast before the start of your next turn, allowing that spell to be cast without any Verbal or Somatic components.

magic.name: Crown of the Keppmir King
magic.desc:
This platinum crown is adorned with black gems and shells. While you wear the crown, you have Resistance to Cold damage and can breathe underwater. Also, your Constitution is 20 while you wear the crown, unless it is 20 or higher without it.

Curse. This crown is cursed, a fact revealed only when an Identify spell is cast on the crown or you attune to it. Attuning to the crown curses you until you are targeted by the Remove Curse spell or similar magic; it is impossible to remove the crown. While cursed, you turn into a keppmir after 2d10 days.

magic.name: Ebon Armor of Invulnerability
magic.desc:
This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.

The Plate Armor of an Ebon Knight roils with the energy of undying evil. Someone who has proficiency with Smith's Tools can melt the armor of three Ebon Knights to make Armor of Invulnerability that also grants Resistance to Necrotic damage. However, this wicked armor requires an attuned wearer to sacrifice life force to it. After the wearer finishes a Long Rest, or the first time they put the armor on after having not worn it while finishing one or more Long Rests, they must either give up one-quarter of their remaining Hit Dice to the armor (rounded up) or increase their Exhaustion level by 1. Someone proficient with Smith's Tools takes 30 days to make this armor, which requires other materials worth 10,000 GP to craft. The intended first wearer must give blood each day, losing Hit Dice or taking Exhaustion levels as if wearing the armor. The process fails, consuming half the materials, if the wearer doesn't feed the armor as it's made. If this being then fails to wear and feed the armor daily for 30 days after it's complete, it disintegrates into ash and smoke.

The wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

If the wearer has a Strength score lower than 15, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

magic.name: Elixir of Life Protection
magic.desc: After you drink this thick, chalky mixture, your Hit Point maximum cannot be reduced for 10 minutes.

magic.name: Enchanted Feather (GH:MG'24)
